rows.label: dromedary
rows.desc:
A large land mammal adapted to arid environments. Domesticated since ancient times, its leather is exceptionally good at insulating against the desert heat, and its milk is quite nourishing. It can be used as a pack animal and mount, but its bouncing gait makes it slower to ride than a horse.

By storing water in its large humps and reclaiming moisture from its breath as it exhales, it can go weeks without drinking.

When in a caravan, people can ride dromedaries to increase the caravan's speed.

rows.label: needlepost
rows.desc:
A cactus genetically modified to give it sentience. The first iteration of this creature was supposed to be a stationary tactical deterrent (the Whip Cactus), but having no intelligence or mobility crippled its effectiveness. With a little genetic engineering, it was given a mobile body, an infantile intelligence, and toxic barbs for good measure. The result backfired as commands proved ineffective. The facility was promptly overrun by the experiments; and a horde of angry cacti escaped into the wilderness.

Needleposts can derive nutrition from very small amounts of rotting vegetables, but they need a huge amount of sunlight (or equivalent) over anything else. Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse is usually fatal to them.

rows.label: razorjack
rows.desc:
The Razorjack is a very aggressive and adaptable creature with a strange body plan: a dual-jawed mouth that leads to two separate but intertwined digestive systems, each of them adapted to consume different types of food. This arrangement makes them extremely energy-efficient, and require very little food. Although it might seem canine at first, its genome has more in common with rodents, with some unusual genetic splicing thrown into the mix. Wounds caused by Razorjacks tend to get infected very easily.

Razorjacks can live in the most desolate conditions, since their need for food is very low. The most ferocious Razorjacks are specially trained, bred and further mutated into fearsome warbeasts, known as Razortooth, used by Feral warlords as terrifying warhounds. (Original concept for the Razortooth by Rooki12k, in the Rimsenal: Feral mod)

rows.label: hawk-bat
rows.desc: Hawk-bats were predatory reptavians with a curved beak and leathery wings that could be found on urbanized worlds like Coruscant and Taris. To get on a hawk-bat's bad side could be very dangerous. As a result, very few lived in captivity. Though they favored granite slugs, hawk-bats would feed on almost anything smaller than themselves. When they hatched from their eggs, young hawk-bats had scaly green skin and were precocial, meaning they were fully independent and able to hunt upon the day of hatching. Upon reaching maturity, the hawk-bat would shed its green skin and emerge with mature purplish-gray skin.

rows.label: teratogenic originator
rows.desc:
This amorphous, flesh coloured, translucent creature seems to lack everything but the most basic instincts, moving around slowly and sometimes devouring any plant it comes in contact with, incorporating it into its cytoplasm. There are some chunks of seemingly normal flesh floating inside it.

Teratogenic Originators are basically an enormous clonal colony of pluripotent stem cells, capable of differentiating into different tissues. They were engineered by a group of unethical scientists as a cheap way to create lab-grown limbs suitable for transplants, but the end results is less than ideal. These strange mutant limbs can be periodically excised from the creature and used at will. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

rows.label: aerofleet
rows.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path. One of the few rare creatures around here that strangely isn’t out for human blood. Well, isn’t that nice?

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, Aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

Aerofleets slowly produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as Blue Gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound, and potentially used to build powerful batteries and generators, with the appropriate research (Biofuel refining, Batteries and Advanced Fabrication).

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.label: wildpawn
rows.desc:
Wildpawns are a variant of the wildpods that have adapted to life outside of swamps and rainforests. Since they have less access to water and rotting vegetation, they grow much less, and are much less dangerous. Wildpawns are less resistant to gunfire, but retain the weakness to fire of their bigger brethren. Wildpawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

Although risky, the Wildpawns can be hunted or farmed for small amounts of edible raw fungus.

With its six legs, the Megatardi is an impressive sight, and its gentle nature makes it a popular pack animal among those brave enough to venture into the polluted world. Though it is easily tamed, the Megatardi is not without its dangers. Upon its death, it releases a cloud of toxic gas, making it a potential hazard for anyone nearby. Despite this, the Megatardi remains a valuable asset for those willing to take on the challenges of the polluted wasteland.

rows.desc:
Hellboars are colossal omnivores drawn to blood, rot and abandoned flesh. They are not pure predators, but their constant hunger and brute strength make them willing to chase live prey when carrion and scraps grow scarce.

The greatest danger of a Hellboar is not only the impact of its charge, but its infectious bite. Its mouth carries enough filth, bacteria and rotting matter to turn a small wound into a serious threat. Its liver, however, concentrates aggressive compounds used by tribes in preparations that can purge toxins and pain at a harsh physical cost.

Perhaps they descend from daeodonts reintroduced into war zones, where corpses, biological waste and broken ecosystems favored the worst traits of the lineage. The Hellboar of today does not seem designed to kill; it seems adapted to survive what is left after.

Sivatherium are imposing herbivores of Earth's ancient megafauna, colossi of muscle and bone marked by thick necks and branching horns like bony crowns. Roaming open plains and forest edges, they command respect even among large predators.

Although generally peaceful, threatened adults can become living walls of bone and muscle. Their carcasses yield large amounts of megabone, and their horns are valued for special refinements and bio-reactive research materials.

The Sivatherium seems to belong to the same ambitions that returned megasloths to the frontier: glitterworld-scale ecological restoration, built with animals too large to disappear easily. The result is a living relic, less a common wild animal and more a survivor of an old attempt to rebuild entire ecosystems.

rows.label: fission mouse, second generation
rows.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

The fission mouse is yet another example of human genetic engineering gone terribly wrong. Presumably, the objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a really unexpected side effect: when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are also harmful to the creature itself. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

This fission mouse is of second generation, indicating the fission process has happened once recently, making it weaker.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

Set loose in the Rim, the raptors are usually short-lived, since they depend on their human owners for survival, their violent instincts having been bred out of them long ago. They are however excellent companions, and they are quite pretty (mechanics-wise, a pedigreed raptor will increase by 15% the beauty of any room it is present at).

Agaripawns are less resistant to gunfire than Agaripods, but retain the weakness to fire of their bigger brethren. Agaripawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so their children are completely wild and independent of them, with no concept of parenthood. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

Although risky, the Agaripawn can be hunted or farmed for small amounts of edible raw agarilux, which can be eaten raw and lasts a bit more than regular fungus.

There are tales of a stoneborn king who fought countless battles on the back of a dwarven muffton. This legend gave rise to a tradition among certain clans, in which upon reaching puberty each stoneborn would be given a baby muffton.

Gigantelopes were once designed as bigger, more powerful variants of the muffalo. An ideal pack beast that carries more weight than their body mass would usually allow. While they are mammals, Gigantelopes have pneumatized bones, meaning they have hollow spaces within them: pneumatized bones are strong, dense and sturdy without being heavy.

The gigantelope has a variable carrying capacity, set by their genome at birth, and colonies around the Rim have been breeding gigantelopes for decades to achieve the perfect specimen.

rows.desc:
A strange chimera between a bear and mole, Groundrunners originally came from Cave Worlds. They were used as walking heavy tools by the locals when they hit parts that plasteel can’t break, and for hauling large boulders that their owners can’t lift.

Due to their domesticated origins, they are surprisingly docile and easy to tame. Their incredible strength and sharp claws allows them to break rocks with relative ease. But out here in the Rim, those claws are usually reserved for ripping power armors apart along with their wearers.

Groundrunners will happily help your colonists mine rocks and minerals. They are however quite lazy and get distracted easily (this interaction requires the Groundrunner to be trained in Haul). This interaction should also work with the Quarry mod.

Trolls spread quickly and are considered a dangerous pest as they frequently attack caravans and travelers. However their hide and delicious meat makes them a target of many hunters.

While excellent livestock, they were ill-suited to serve as mounts, guards, or attack animals. . Jakobeasts were introduced by colonists that sought herd animals capable of defending themselves. As a result of the settlers' efforts, the creatures spread to hundreds of worlds, occasionally surviving long after the settlers themselves had vanished into history. Wild jakobeasts were hunted for their horns, which supposedly possess mysterious properties.

These creatures though tricky to domesticate had both the build and strength to make them perfect beasts of burden. The Royal House of Naboo kept a herd of Gualaar that were used to carry state officials. This regal affiliation and their physical practicality meant they were exported and ultimately spread across multiple worlds. It's similarity in appearance to the legendary Thrumbo is a point of interest amongst several xenobiologists.

rows.desc:
This lumbering mass of apparently decomposing plant matter is a Wildpod, a sentient mycoid creature native to some jungle infested planet on the Rim. The Wildpod is almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass without doing much damage, but very weak to fire. Interestingly, it reproduces asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

Although risky, the Wildpod can be hunted or farmed for decent amounts of edible raw fungus.

rows.label: worhin
rows.desc:
Worhins are colossal beasts of the glacial plains, clad in golden-gray wool and carried by bodies heavy enough to cross snow, ice and open ground without hesitation. From a distance they seem like great herd herbivores; up close, they are living walls of muscle, wool and horn.

In the present, colonies that manage to domesticate them use Worhins as heavy pack animals and beasts of war. Their size, appetite and handling make them difficult to raise, but few animals can match their ability to break lines, carry weight and turn improvised defenses into rubble. When butchered, they yield valuable wool, resilient hide, dense meat and the Brontorhin, their fossilized horn.

Perhaps the Worhin began as a piece of glacial biodiversity, made to keep cold ecosystems in motion, open paths through snow and sustain chains of life where almost nothing prospered. Today, adapted to the frontier and colony wars, that ancient ecological function survives as brute force.

Megaloceros is an easily angered herbivore that can cause severe wounds with its extraordinarily large antlers, which are otherwise used exclusively for attracting females.

rows.label: tetra slug
rows.desc:
These massive slugs are a common sight among Glitterworld controlled territories, where they lumber about as glorified power plants. Outside of one, they are deployed as a mobile power source for Glitterworld research expeditions. It is rare to see one without the iconic power cores that protrude from their backs, as their unique bodily chemical composition is capable of outputting power that far surpasses any known natural sources. Thus, they are widely valued by every technologically developing civilization throughout the galaxy.

While a gentle giant that would prefer to run away instead of fight, modified slugs come armoured with plasteel shells, quad cores that can act as Tesla cannons, and a Tactical AI inserted within the brain that takes over and makes no hesitation to use all of its armament to obliterate any perceived threat within vicinity.

Properly outfitted Tetra slugs will slowly recharge batteries on their vicinity (most modded batteries are supported).

Sadly they can’t be trained but will happily hunt smaller prey that happen to wander into their territory or fight back against any foolish predators. rows.desc:
A wispy-looking creature that is the only known example of plasma-based life in the Rim: the Aurora Sylph is of artificial origins, and its biology is so strange that only the most advanced glitterworld technology could have been responsible for its creation. It is believed that the sylphs were created as a lifeform capable of surviving in the atmosphere of Red Dwarf stars, for utterly inscrutable purposes. They don't seem to be affected by gravity much, so they can also be found stranded in the gravity well of a planet.

Sylphs are immune to temperature extremes, though very fragile and easy to damage. They don't need to eat, as they will replenish their energy simply by absorbing light. If they are content, they will periodically influence the magnetic fields of a planet, and cause beautiful auroras, hence their name.

These creatures once served as the frontline skirmishers of an insectoid hive; A collection of genetically modified insects made as a weapon against Mechanoid invasions. Their job consisted of reducing lone Mechanoid infantry to Swiss cheese; And they were good at it. Even the mighty Centipede was no match against the swarm of spikes.

Nowadays, they can be found roaming in packs that are a joke compared to their former numbers and with killer instincts that yearn to be reawakened once more.

rows.label: darkbeast
rows.desc:
The darkbeast is a mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with metallic spikes housing a distributed cloud of sun-blocking mechanites.

These deployable mechanite clouds can cover a huge region, blanketing it in darkness, and it is thought that the darkbeast was created as a terrorist weapon that attacks settlements by depriving them of sunlight, affecting their agricultural yields. Darkbeasts have naturally evolved over the centuries making them extremely unstable, and they will only release enough mechanites upon death. Thankfully, predators usually give them a wide berth.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.label: windbeast
rows.desc:
The windbeast is a mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with fleshy tentacles housing a distributed net of weather-affecting mechanites.

These deployable mechanite swarms have the ability to affect the weather in a localized manner, creating pressure gradients that may evolve into full-blown hurricane winds. This effect is used offensively by the creature, and is specially dangerous if it is killed, as the large sudden release of all mechanites can cause a tornado. Thankfully, predators usually give them a wide berth and they are quite rare.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: slurrypede
rows.desc:
Although rare, mechanoids have been known to capture prisoners, and the Slurrypede is their solution to feed them in the most efficient way possible. The Slurrypede is a modified bio-mechanoid capable of devouring almost anything and processing it into a homogeneous organic slurry. This slurry is edible for carnivore and omnivore animals, but barely, and completely indigestible for herbivores.

Slurrypedes are docile, almost never hostile, and in case a mechanoid base is destroyed and one of them manages to survive, they tend to roam the wilderness aimlessly, consuming any organic material in their path and turning it into nutrient paste.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: live plants, trees, fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: muffalope
rows.desc:
A very naughty hybrid that can be told to relieve itself on command, creating puddles of chemfuel-infused urine around it. For those who just want to watch the world burn in the most vulgar way.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. A bit too slow for a caravan companion but make up for it with intelligence and an unusual chemfuel ability that lends itself for defence.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All primary muffalo hybrids have 150% carrying capacity on caravans.

specials.text: can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: ravager
rows.desc:
This large, genetically-engineered insectoid is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The Ravager was conceived as a space-bound bioweapon. Drop pods filled to the brim with Ravagers would be launched towards unsuspecting mechanoid ships, and the fearsome insectoids would rip through the ship's plating and lay waste to any mechanoid inside. Ravagers proved to be too unreliable, though, and the geneline was scrapped.

Several Ravagers can be seen today in derelict spaceships, stations and asteroids, as well as aimlessly roaming the countryside throughout the Rim. They are mostly adapted to their solitary life in space.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Causes additional damage when fighting against mechanoids.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: morrak
rows.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Gomphotaria is equipped with not two, but four huge tusks that it uses to hammer and pierce its prey with.
Their seal-like bodies allow them to move very swiftly underwater but their huge mass as well as a lack of legs renders them somewhat sluggish on land.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: thrumffalo
rows.desc:
One of the largest creatures in existence, dwarfing even the thrumbo and the mighty Gallatross. Capable of transporting a massive amount of material, producing a luxurious and excellent wool as well as thick, nutritious milk, they are almost the perfect farm animal. That is as long as you don’t look at your feed costs and die of a heart attack, but the scientists that designed this hybrid never had to worry about such things. Food is something for the proles to worry about.

A colossal hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Completely herbivorous and with an appetite large enough to cause even large colonies to starve within a single season. This hybrid can prove worth the food costs as it produces thick, delicious milk every couple of days as well as luxurious wool every couple of seasons. Slightly more dimwitted than its progenitor and will attempt to wander off in search of food if not kept penned up.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor.

specials.text: can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: chickenlope
rows.desc:
The ideal companion for those who love the smell of fried eggs and napalm in the morning. Regretfully they’re far too birdbrained to receive any direction, and most owners have been noted saying “I’ve made a huge mistake”.

An avian hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Very dangerous if allowed to breed uncontrollably, so consider liberal fireproofing and selling the excess. Produces chemfuel daily as well as an egg every 2 days.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: squirralope
rows.desc:
It’s small, it’s cute, it’s a ticking time bomb waiting for some idiot to think it looks delicious. It’s not going to be a big explosion, but that doesn’t matter much when it’s in your mouth.

A rodent hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Small, weak but fast, this hybrid suits those looking for a fuel production method in a small package. Produces chemfuel much more efficiently compared to a boomalope but it needs to be milked every day.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All rodent hybrids have fast gestation, as long as a fertility unblocker was used when creating them in the genomorpher.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: needlechicken
rows.desc:
This abomination is part chicken, part sentient cactus. If cactus nuggets weren't a thing, they are now. You can think of them as solar-powered egg layers.

Useful abilities: Needlechicken are decent egg layers. They can defend themselves with tiny poison barb attacks, and they almost don't need sustenance (except for a large amount of sunlight).

specials.text: feeds on light instead of food

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: catalope
rows.desc:
Have you ever wanted to have a cat that could start fires with hairballs? No? Too bad, this one does and if you’re unlucky it’ll be outside when it’s hunting. Which won’t be often, because those fuel sacs make for a surprisingly efficient energy reserve. Exploding kittens is no longer just a game, it’s a hazard warning.

A feline hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Intelligent, low maintenance with a weak ranged flame attack, they make for an unusual companion. 

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability, which in the case of these small animals is ideal to get out of a fight.

specials.text: spawns already carrying a permanent condition
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: stoneback
rows.desc:
These large reptile-like animals normally feed on the likes of cacti. If angered, however, their durable hide makes them quite difficult to kill.

Their longer back legs and strange appearance lends credence to the belief that they were engineered to live in arid environments. Why they live underground, however, is uncertain.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: black scribe
rows.desc:
A shade amongst the scorching sands. The black scribe is a deadly insectoid capable of taking down creatures much larger than itself with its dreadful sting. The name of scribe comes from its feather-like stinger, composed of countless small quills that it uses to quickly inject a toxic venom, which greatly weakens its prey.

It’s venom can be safely extracted every few days, and while the toxin is incredibly dangerous, it procures a sensastion of bliss when consumed in small doses. Making it a highly sought-after drug.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: jellypot
rows.desc: Named the jellypot for its ability to produce insect jelly in its large thoracic sac, this rare animal is almost exclusively found near insectoid hives. Despite being farmed much like ants do with aphids, it does not seem capable of breeding in captivity.

specials.text: can be placed dormant, asleep until triggered
lies dormant until something wakes it, then all of them wake
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: bogwing
rows.desc: The bogwing is a fast flying reptavian native to Dagobah. They could be found on a number of worlds located across the galaxy. They mostly fed on small creatures dwelling in the lower levels of tree canopies (including rodents like leaftails) to avoid larger predators.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: meganeura
rows.desc:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest flying insect to ever exist, meganeura, just like modern dragonflies, is a highly specialised predator.
Swift and agile, it used to have no aerial competition, which was one of the reasons why it had evolved to be so gigantic.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: bumbledrone queen
rows.desc:
The Bumbledrone is a mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a Bumbledrone isn't very powerful, more a nuisance than a threat, but if threatened in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. "Luckily", since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method.

This particular bumbledrone seems to be a "queen", so called because it seems to deposit eggs from which other bumbledrones may hatch. It tends to do this specially once it has settled into an environment it considers safe, so it might be a really useful asset to tame it.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

specials.text: migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: splicetoot
rows.desc: A small, bloated mutant that crawls awkwardly on underdeveloped limbs, resembling a grotesque parody of a toddler. Its enlarged belly sloshes with rotstink gas, swelling and trembling with each jerking movement. Upon reaching its victim, the fragile body ruptures in a violent explosion, releasing a choking cloud of dangerous gas. Whether it was once a child or simply shaped to mock one is a cruelty too dreadful to think about.
rows.diet: nothing — it does not eat

rows.label: boomsquirrel
rows.desc:
With adorable horns and long snoots, these squeaky lads are ideal in giving your enemy a stunning surprise. Their chemfuel mixture includes other gases that create a blinding and disorienting flashbang when remotely detonated. They’ll still make a regular boom if killed though.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Quite fast and intelligent, these hybrids work as excellent swarm attackers. Their rapid reproduction cycle and stunning explosion make for an ideal companion to ranged masters.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: toxalope
rows.desc: A pollution-adapted cousin of the boomalope, the toxalope grows toxic pouches on its back. When it dies, the toxic material explodes and produces a deadly toxic cloud. Unlike the boomalope, the toxalope cannot be milked.

specials.text: bursts into a toxic cloud on death
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: boombeetle
rows.desc:
For lovers of xenomorphs everywhere, this bomb-ass bombadier is ready to launch sacs of acidic chemfuel at your enemies for fun and profit. Don’t expect a second pair of jaws though, that mouth is for spitting only.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Quite temperamental for a hybrid, but they prove to be worth it as they store caustic chemfuel in their sacs which can then be lobbed at a distance. Practically useless in melee, so keep them safe and provide fire support. Can be ordered to detonate auxiliary acid sacs as a defensive measure, but that will also self-harm.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: boomsnake
rows.desc:
What happens when you mix a spitting cobra, a rattlesnake and a creature designed to lactate refined fuel? This abomination, that’s what. Drive it into a corner and it’ll hurt itself to release deadly neurotoxins. Try and keep your distance and it’ll spit toxic blood right at you. Clearly someone was a sore loser in playing pretend games as a child, but had either the brains or the money to prove themselves right.

A reptile hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Decently intelligent with a nasty bite and even nastier ranged attack, both causing toxic buildup. Quite a high metabolism which supports its various combat abilities, best suited for home defence.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: manwolf
rows.desc:
Possibly either the ancestor to the warg or an attempt at creating a successor, the team in charge of making this particular hybrid clearly had read one to many mythological novels. Arguably there’s no transformation at the full moon, so you just get the permanent single form, but there’s no pleasing some people.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive canine genes. A fast and dangerous hunter with almost misplaced self-confidence. Also very intelligent and possessing faint regenerative capabilities. Extremely hardy but also extremely restrictive in their diet.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts.

specials.text: heals its own wounds over time
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses

rows.label: boomalope paragon
rows.desc:
While more of a risk to keep around, they are considerably more efficient and don’t eat your crops as much. Plus their permanent sad expression just makes you want to pet them, how can you say no.

A perfect boomalope animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon produces deepchem instead and explodes on death in a much more violent fashion.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: boomffalo
rows.desc:
People love efficiency and having one thing to cover all their needs. Well this isn’t it, but it gets damn close. The chemfuel sacs have mixed with milk-producing glands, which make for a milk that smells like pure gasoline and could almost power a vehicle.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Has a large appetite due to it producing multiple products, namely deepchem, thin wool and an unusual milk that shares properties with Chemshine.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: cactus crab
rows.desc: A smaller relative of the crystal crab, adapted to desert-like underground environments. They grow cacti on their shell for camoflauge and defense. From birth, they find a rock and settle into it as their shell.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: boomabear
rows.desc:
Originally intended as a way to make boomalopes more combat viable, their powerful muscles have instead been focused on compressing its produced chemfuel as a way to store greater amounts of chemfuel without care of how dangerous it is.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Consumes more than twice as much compared to a boomalope but produces deepchem instead. They’re also capable of defending themselves should any predator be foolish enough to go after them.

specials.text: produces a harvestable resource on a timer

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: toraton
rows.desc: Due to its sheer size, an adult toraton has no predators and no longer has any need for a shell. Small sections of the ancestoral shell do remain, however, forming an external support for the creature's muscles, which its feeble ribs and vertebrae alone cannot carry.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count
can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: wraid
rows.desc: Wraids were large reptilian creatures found on many desert planets across the galaxy (including but not limited to Tatooine, Ruhnuk, Korriban and even Tython). They were carnivorous creatures, relying on scavening and ambush to find their prey. Wraids were often over hunted for their valuable hides, causing their populations to spike and fall.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: dinornis
rows.desc:
Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The tallest birds to ever exist. They belong to the moa family and are characterised by quite dramatic sexual dimorphism, with the females being significantly larger than the males
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: flesh growth
rows.desc: Something went terribly wrong. A huge and weird growth has spawned within the electrowomb, breaking it completely and spreading all around. This growth is a hatchery for small flies that can devour any living creature to the bone. It seems to be sensitive to daylight, but no one knows how far it can spread at night.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: mature fleshbeast
rows.desc:
The unwanted result of a genetic experiment gone wrong, fleshbeasts are usually miserable, weak creatures that ooze pus and struggle to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a fleshbeast manages to survive, and even thrive. Perhaps it was foolishly released into the wild, where it managed to stabilize and grow. Or perhaps it was stronger than average, and managed to subdue and devour its imprudent creators. In any case, it has now turned into a pulsating, fleshy behemoth with a ravenous appetite.

Mature fleshbeasts swallow their prey whole, storing up to 5 creatures on its huge stomach for later consumption. Prey may survive for up to one day, but they'll later be consumed and expelled as skeletized remains.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses

rows.label: polluwog
rows.desc: The larval form of the gastro toad. It lives in the disgusting waters of polluted biomes, feeding off any detritus and plants it can reach. It often lives in large groups.

specials.text: grows into a different creature at a set age
feeds off the sea or lake bed
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: batbird
rows.desc: An engineered hybrid of mammal and avian, the batbird lives in shallow caves below the desert sands. It feeds on small prey and gives birth to live young.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: fission mouse
rows.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

The fission mouse is yet another example of human genetic engineering gone terribly wrong. Presumably, the objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a really strange side effect: when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are also harmful to the creature itself. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: tainted turtle
rows.desc: A mutated turtle that can withstand the noxious waters of polluted biomes. It cannot however survive its own toxin-filled sacs bursting due to high stress.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: cave cricket
rows.desc: While often considered a pest to cave-dwellers, some have domesticated these meaty crickets for their own use as disgusting but hearty food. They grow fast and lay a multitude of eggs in mere days.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: plasmorph
rows.desc:
This bizarre, mutant snail has a very strange way of defending itself against predators. Inside its armoured shell made of iron sulphide, specialized organs along the Plasmorph's body generate an electric discharge similar to those found in electric eels. This discharge is very low voltage, not powerful enough to damage most creatures. However, the Plasmorph uses it as a spark to ignite its own flammable spit, and lob it at its prey.

Such a strange mechanism is surely not natural, but what was its intended purpose is a mystery lost to the ages.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: manscarab
rows.desc:
They say you can learn a lot by taking something apart and putting it back together again. Not this creature, it doesn’t give a damn, it just wants to take things apart because the hardest part is someone else’s problem. Some people actually prefer these chitinous creatures over actual humans as they’re not going to use up good material in a botched attempt.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Easy to train, quite resilient but not a great combatant. This particular hybrid fills the niche of fulfilling deconstruction orders around the colony, freeing up otherwise valuable manpower.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them. Menscarab will take building deconstruction orders around the colony.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: mutating tumorfish
rows.desc: The adult form of the tumorfish. Now adapted to an amphibious lifestyle, it can hunt in water as well as on land. Despite still being quite fishy, it can move with surprising dexterity out of water.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: narkospider
rows.desc:
Narkospiders are massive subterranean spiders that hunt by ambush, preferring to sedate prey rather than overpower it through brute force. They wait in tunnels and dark spaces until a target comes close enough for a narcotic bite.

Their venom causes deep narkosis, reducing movement and perception until the victim can no longer respond. This makes the creature less explosive than other predators, but especially dangerous in caves, corridors and poorly lit fights, where a single bite can decide the encounter.

It is difficult to say whether the Narkospider is a planned lineage or an extreme subterranean adaptation. Its body seems made to control territory without wasting energy: immobilize, neutralize and wait.

can be drafted and ordered like a colonist

rows.label: fungal mimic mantis
rows.desc: A native to the fungal forest caverns, this mantis is larger than a person. It uses its fungus-covered carapace as camouflage while hunting. Unlike other mantises, they rely on their attacks injecting anesthetic and poisonous chemicals into prey.

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: energy spider
rows.desc: Energy spiders (or "spice spiders") were horrifying arachnids that inhabited the Spice Mines of Kessel. The webs that these creatures spin between their legs can be harvested as Glitterstim (a potent drug and medicinal ingredient). This variety of Energy Spider appears to have been bioengineered to survive off of Kessel but with the downside that they have massive appetites. They can however survive in extreme temperatures (both hot and cold) and they (or their product) are not aversed to the sunlight.

lies dormant until something wakes it, then all of them wake
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: smoldersting scorpion
rows.desc: This colossal scorpion is found only in the deepdest depths of the earth. It uses its burning venom to cook its prey alive from the inside out.

specials.text: can be placed dormant, asleep until triggered
lies dormant until something wakes it, then all of them wake
predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: maguana
rows.desc: The patterning on the skin of this relative of the surface iguana resembles both cooled and hot magma, seemingly to blend in with the volatile environment within the cavern systems. They are naturally immune to fire due to the special composition of their flesh.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: crystal crab
rows.desc: A large and powerful relative of the decorator crab, cavern crystals grow from the minerals on this crab's rocky shell. Despite its strong exoskeleton, the crystal crab hauls around this heavy shell, the reason for which is unknown. They are not known to breed in captivity.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: foundry beetle
rows.desc: While herbivorous, this beetle is no easy prey. It uses its massive mandibles to crush both rival mates and anything that tries to hunt it. These beetles are often bred as war bugs by the more vicious cave dwellers.

specials.text: can be placed dormant, asleep until triggered
lies dormant until something wakes it, then all of them wake
can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: royal rhino beetle
rows.desc: A gigantic type of rare beetle that is revered by certain underground cultures for its rarity and power. While its royal purple chitin is beautiful, it is also extremely durable. The extremely sharp horn gracing their head fetches a high price. While normally gentle by nature, it is extremely dangerous when enraged.

specials.text: can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, trees, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: pod worm
rows.desc: Though large and intimidating, the appearance of this strange insectoid-like creature does not match with its otherwise passive nature. While it typically lives in insectoid hives as a part of the glow pod producing caste, it occasionally wanders off or gets captured and sold by humanoids.

specials.text: can be placed dormant, asleep until triggered
lies dormant until something wakes it, then all of them wake

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: tooke
rows.desc: Tooke were small, hopping rodents native to the planet Naboo. They were nocturnal by nature and like all rodents, the tooke had a high reproductive rate and they generally fed on nuts and berries. They were a common pest animal that spread readily to many worlds including Stoga, where predators like the worrt would gorge themselves immobile consuming them. Even a carnivorous plant (the so-called the 'tooke-trap') had evolved to target these creatures by emitting it's mating pheremone; however the rodents were usually agile enough to escape.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count
migrates across the map in herds

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: needleroll
rows.desc:
Needlerolls are needleposts that have evolved to grow in the most arid and dry environments in the Rim.

Needleposts need almost no sustenance, absorbing all the energy they need from sunlight and minute amounts of water that they extract from morning dew. Like needleposts, they need a huge amount of sunlight (or equivalent). Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse could be fatal to them.

Megathrisp uses sharp mandibles to rip the armor into shreds, while overcharged acid glands coat the exposed flesh in corrosive substance, causing severe burns. In close quarters, the sharp horns and ripper-blades will dispose of flesh and metal alike. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

While fuel itself is not dangerous, a single spark is enough to set the area on fire. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

Dunealisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs stun and burn anyone they touch, allowing the Dunealisk to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

The lava flea would then continue digesting rocks and other nutrients, shedding its protective shell with time. Lava fleas were also very suitable mounts and exported as such to worlds with inhospital climates to other creatures.

rows.label: insectoid paragon
rows.desc:
A terrifying callback to the original Sorne geneline, this mobile hive was originally designed to engage the mechanoid enemy head-on. By carrying an entire colony of insects with hardened mandibles, their ability to practically disassemble the mechanical menace proved just as effective at turning against their human overlords.

A perfect insectoid animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon is extremely intelligent and carries a dangerous brood of warrior flies. A burst of pheromones summons the drones to protect their hive and queen, shredding apart all other nearby creatures.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them. Insect clouds ability: twice a day it can create insect clouds around it that damage any animal crossing them, except insectoid paragons, which are immune.

A broodmother to the insects in her hive, the princess doesn’t do heavy work, and tries to avoid combat if possible. As massive as an adult thrumbo, the princess instills fear in most opponents. Her thick chitinous armor makes her hard to kill, whilst long, deadly blades can tear through plasteel shielding in seconds. Despite being quite slow in open terrain, an insectoid princess is capable of creating new swarmlings at a rapid pace, and should never be allowed to settle down.

The war wyrm was originally an infant exogorth that had been mutated and warped by Sith alchemy. They were very rare and very large and several specimens were believed to have been left behind by Sith armies on various worlds having fulfilled their roles as apex siege beasts.

They were found on many worlds having stowed away in supplies and once escaping establishing themselves in the wild.

rows.label: crescendo anole
rows.desc:
Most of the time, the Crescendo Anole is a harmless iguanian lizard that feeds on vegetation and small arthropods. They are unusually intelligent, and can be kept as pets. However, when the anole becomes aggressive in any way, usually in self defense, an unstable cocktail of growth hormones and biomechanical mechanites causes a runaway growth of the creature's cells, turning it into a hulking crocodilian nightmare.

This effect is temporary, lasting a few hours, and afterwards the anole must recover its strength to be able to go through it again, becoming extremely hungry in the interim.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

Living primarily in water, two of its heads remain submerged while only one absorbs oxygen. Quick and vicious in its attacks, the Hydra's bite is lethal, delivering a potent venom with each strike. Its ability to adapt to even the harshest of environments makes it a formidable predator, and one that should be approached with caution. The Hydra's three heads are a symbol of its adaptability and resilience, making it a force to be reckoned with in the polluted biomes.

The Erin (Hyaena Erinae), also commonly known as a Corpsemouth, is a disgusting genetically modified hyena with reptilian characteristics. Erins were created as a perfect scavenger, greatly preferring to feed on already dead animals than hunting them, although if no corpses are present they will resort to hunting their own prey or consuming butchered meat.

.Erins will receive a considerable health boost if consuming fresh corpses that they didn't have to kill, making them both great at corpse disposal and as front line attackers if they are properly fed. Furthermore, they have the ability to regurgitate stomach acids as a dangerous ranged attack.

rows.label: junglelisk
rows.desc:
The Junglelisk is a mutant variation of the Feralisk, adapted to living in the deepest, darkest jungles of the Rim. Some even say that the Junglelisk is the original breed of Lisks from which all the others originate. They certainly reproduce fast enough for this to be the case, and female junglelisks can be fertilized once and store the genetic material to lay eggs for quite a long time.

Junglelisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs stun and cover with acid anyone they touch, allowing the Junglelisk to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

rows.label: Sporemole
rows.desc:
Sporemoles are monstrous descendants of ancient burrowing moles, deformed by their parasitic relationship with the Mycorgloom fungus. Their bodies serve as living soil for glowing fungal growths, making them larger, tougher and far harder to kill than any ordinary subterranean animal.

Once insect-eaters, they became opportunistic carnivores. They ambush prey from tunnels, defend burrows brutally, and may surface alone when hunger forces them out of the ground. Their meat smells strongly of mold, and few colonists forget the first encounter with a creature that seems half mammal, half fungal colony.

The Sporemole may not have been created as a weapon or livestock, but as the living accident of a contaminated ecosystem. Where Mycorgloom spreads, the line between animal, fungus and burrow begins to disappear.

rows.label: crocorse
rows.desc:
A rather muscular hybrid with an impressively long snout, this ravenous reptile combines adaptability with mobility. Unusually, its terrifyingly long maw filled with curved teeth is not used to tear flesh to eat but to imbue toxins and the required muscles to spray those toxins out. This means they have to eat a lot more due to their subpar digestive system and their favourite activities include lounging in the sun and moving with disturbing quickness when the dinner bell is sounded. Also it… kinda looks like a weird shoe if you look at it, but, uh, don’t put your foot in there.

An equine hybrid with recessive reptile genes. A rather slow hybrid for its category, its main advantage is that it is very durable and it has a ranged toxic breath attack. Quite durable and comfortable in a wide range of temperatures, they present a hidden danger for those foolish enough to attack an otherwise easy target.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM.

rows.desc:
Milking snakes for venom in order to create medicine is an extremely dangerous career. While this particular beast of burden proved to be capable in other areas, it was mainly synthesised in order to provide a safer way of sourcing an anaesthetic coagulant to be used in emergencies. Or someone was trying to get high by milking a reptilian space cow, who really knows.

A reptile hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. A strong pack animal with a massive appetite and a proportionate filth rate. Quite durable and will prove a fatal mistake for any animal that attempts to hunt them, as their fangs, horns and claws are all venomous. Can be milked every ten days for a vial of paralysing coagulant, best used for large animals that are suffering from multiple lacerations.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks.

rows.label: thrumbolizard
rows.desc:
About as close as anyone has ever gotten in making a recreation of dragons from folklore. Capable of surviving in extreme cold or heat, the only thing really missing is a pair of wings and an innate desire to hoard piles of gold for a nest. That and the fact that it isn’t carnivorous, instead having an appetite for vegetables and wood fibres.

A colossal hybrid with recessive reptile genes. With a mouth dripping with venom and tough, flexible scales covering the body, this hybrid makes for a nasty and incredibly durable combat hybrid. If that wasn’t enough, it can also breath out a fog of noxious fumes and move deceptively quickly.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor. All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks.
rows.diet: live plants, trees, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: dusk rat
rows.desc:
A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.

This rat seems to be markedly different from other rats. It is a purely nocturnal animal, and it has four glowing eyes.

rows.label: murkling
rows.desc:
A distant relative of the nightling, murklings are -in fact- quite their opposite. They are not as fierce nor are they proficient hunters, often scavenging in packs for scraps left behind by the more apt predators.  Their most distinctive features are the abnormally elongated structures on their snouts, which are theorized to produce specific vibrational sequences that allow for discrete communication between pack members. Their physical weakness is compensated for with above average intellect, allowing them to outsmart organisms as intelligent as the Forsaken. Their reputation for stealthily stealing supplies across the Rim has earned them the nickname 'thief of the night'.

Special abilities: A Murkling's bite can inflict the bubonic plague. The delicate tendrils on their snouts can dissolve nearby corpses and turn them into semi-liquid carrion that can feed the Murkling.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: fungal husk
rows.desc:
A bloated, shambling corpse animated by a genetically modified strain of caterpillar fungus, used as a biological weapon.

Fungal husks serve as ambulatory delivery systems for the fungus, attempting to reach and maul any living animals nearby to spread the fungal infection. This infection is extremely virulent, able to kill a human being in a few hours. However, it is very easy to treat, and it will be kept contained and disappear as long as a medic treats it fast and with a decent treatment quality. Luckily, the fungus has mutated from its original weaponized effects, and a person or animal dying from the infection won't transform into another fungal husk.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit, fluids; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: nightling
rows.desc:
A sleek predatory beast with rows of quills on its back. The Nightling is a purely nocturnal hunter, hence its name, and isn't at all shy to prey on much larger animals, or people, than itself. Apart from its strong jaws, nightlings can throw the quills on their backs to overpower their prey.

Art by Gon (check more at https://twitter.com/GON_again).

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: muffalorat
rows.desc:
Breeding a muffalo hybrid into such a small package means they have very little capacity for either wool or milk. They’re very quick though, and your handlers better be quicker on their daily milking and shearing.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Very weak as a pack animal but they breed quickly and can be milked and sheared daily. The amount of product is small, but it’s thick wool and nutritious milk.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All primary muffalo hybrids have 150% carrying capacity on caravans.

rows.label: night ave
rows.desc:
A large flightless bird, black as night. It seems to share part of its phenotype with the Nightling, hinting that they both originate from the same planet: a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken-. Night Aves have adapted to environments with very low sunlight, and they are purely nocturnal animals.

Night Aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses, and if properly trained they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds (this interaction needs the Giddy-Up, combat mounts mod, and it will make the Night Aves move 50% faster when used as mounts).

rows.label: dusk prowler
rows.desc: A result of failed animal weaponization trials, the dusk prowler is an ideal killing machine, built and modified to satisfy the requirements of fast-paced warfare. The fierce nature of the prowler is reinforced further by the muscular protrusions on their back, which simultaneously act as both accelerators and as weapons. Their capability to overrun even the most well defended military facilities resulted in the systematic purge that was commissioned by the intergalactic federations centuries ago, in hopes of driving the prowlers to extinction. Thus, very few prowler sightings are reported across the Rim nowadays, with those who see one almost never making it out alive to tell the tale.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: muffalopede
rows.desc:
An oversized grub with udders that extrude jelly instead of milk, its hard-headedness serves it well in both getting what it wants and nutting anyone foolish enough to think they’re better than them. Allegedly there was a case where the owner was prevented from shearing the creature for so long that the overlapping plates completely prevented it from moving, who was afterwards thanked with a kick in the nether region.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Higher metabolism compared to other insectoid hybrids as well as stubborn, any predator foolish enough to think of them as an easy meal will be responded with a headbutt like a sledgehammer. Can work as a pack animal but refuses to haul comparatively heavy loads. Regularly produces precious jelly and can be sheared for chitin, which overlaps and protects the animal well from blunt attacks.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

rows.label: snakecat
rows.desc:
Possibly one of the weirdest and cutest snakes to be ever created. They have several tiny legs which are used to push its body along, while also having an invitingly soft fur. Quite a lot of people never stop freaking out from something sliding up the backs of their legs only to get softly headbutted by a purring python.

A reptile hybrid with recessive feline genes. An unusually furry snake that enjoys nuzzling while also hunting for prey much weaker than itself. Incredibly intelligent and easy to train, they combine quick reflexes and an incredibly nasty bite and spitting attack.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks.

rows.label: nightram
rows.desc:
The Nightram is a stubborn herbivore that shares much of its genome with the predatory Nightling, hinting at a common origin. They both originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. When found on other worlds, the Nightram are exclusively nocturnal, instinctively avoiding natural sunlight.

Nightrams are peaceful unless disturbed or threatened.

rows.label: shadow charger
rows.desc:
A creature known for its mighty elongated horns, the Shadow Charger is actually rather passive, their horns only being used upon provocation or during mating. Their name is derived from their aggression against potential rivals during mating season, where the females are seen charging and locking horns with each other to secure a mate. While they were once used as battle mounts due to their speed and ability to ram, nowadays they are mostly reared across the rim for their creamy milk and abundant meat.

Special abilities: Shadow chargers provide very good amounts of milk, and they can defend themselves much better than cows.

rows.label: thunderox
rows.desc:
A creature often seen in the colder reaches of the Rim, the Thunderox is recognized by its shaggy thick fur and stumpy but effective horn. They get their name from their tendency to bray out during the dawn of thunderstorms, which is still used as a signal by farmers and drifters alike to seek refuge. They are reared in several farming colonies in the cold wastelands for their thick milk, comfortable fur and tough but satiating meat.

Special abilities: Besides from being a reliable farm animal that can be sheared for wool and milked, Thunderox are resilient beasts, slowly regenerating their health.

rows.desc:
The Nightmule is a hardy pack beast, used for transporting loads or doing other heavy work. Nightmules originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race know as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. They were domesticated by the Forsaken hundreds of years ago, and can be found roaming around some other planets in the Rim.

Nightmules are stronger than muffalos, though they produce a very low amount of milk, and no wool. Similar to the Nightling, another creature from the Forsaken's planet, their back is crowned by dangerous quills, though the Nightmule lacks the capacity to throw them as defensive weapons.

This was the home planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken, and Crepuscular Beetles were often used as domesticated beasts of burden.

Crepuscular Beetles are active during dusk. They also don't need a lot of rest, expending much less time than other creatures to replenish their energies.

Records indicate that the local indigineous tribes were very resistant to corporate takeover and the megacorp in charge wanted to reduce profit losses. Eventually the planet starved as they were unable to stop these creatures from feasting on farmlands and food reserves.

A colossal hybrid with recessive insectoid genes. A slow moving tank with limited regenerative capabilities, they are almost unkillable if it weren’t for their crippling hunger. As durable as a capital ship, any colony that could possibly support the diet of even a single one would be considered impervious to raids.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor. They are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

Facing an Alpha means facing the living center of the migration. Its natural carapace blunts common weapons, while the amount of plastite inside its body makes it one of the most valuable and dangerous targets a colony can encounter.

An Alpha may not be a planned variant, but the result of decades of biometallic accumulation, environmental pressure and continuous survival. What begins as an animal ends as a walking monument of plastite, bone and age.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with anima vegetation, with several Anima Trees and Mystic Cap mushrooms growing on its back. These plants seem to provide sustenance in a symbiotic relationship with the colossus.

When tamed, the Anima Colossus can be periodically "trimmed" to obtain wood. It will also very rarely produce a huge, hardened anima pearl, which can be planted to grow a new Anima Tree (this interaction requires Royalty).

Of course, the timescales involved are impressive for humans, and a Gallatross might expend as long as two decades roaming around a Graveyard.

After 24 hours, infant Space Worms will hatch from the host, killing them in the process.

Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in some wretched planet of the Rim. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity. Unfortunately for colonies on the Rim, this means batteries...

Drainers undergo metamorphosis like most other lepidopterans, though their larval stage is pretty short, and doesn't have the energy draining abilities of the adults.

rows.label: green goo
rows.desc:
These amorphous, ambulatory masses of gelatinous fluid seem to be a mockery of life. Although they look like individuals, in reality they are part of a greater gelatinous superorganism, with only one objective: grow and expand.

They have been nicknamed green goo due to their ability to reproduce constantly, requiring very little sustenance, and quickly filling all available ecological niches. In the field of eschatology, a grey goo is an end-of-the-world scenario involving molecular nanotechnology in which out-of-control self-replicating robots consume all biomass while building more of themselves. A green goo scenario, however, involves biological self-replicating entities. NOTE: due to gameplay constraints, green goo will only self-replicate until the map holds 40 creatures, because I don't want to fry your computers. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

Experienced quarry overseers often hire hunters to track ironcasket beetle nests, as their shells can be extracted for a hassle-free source of steel.

rows.desc:
Decay Drakes are large, winged flightless lizards that inhabit places with an abundance of vegetation. Decay Drakes release a nauseous cocktail of volatile pheromones that quickly accelerates the rotting process of plants, turning vegetation around them into mounds of fermented organic matter. They will consume these and usually get incredibly drunk in the process. Interestingly, the creature has four separate livers in order to process the huge amounts of alcohol.

They aren't easy to domesticate, but if they can be coerced to accept humans, they might be useful hunting companions, specially if provided with alcohol...

Human beings have been known to consume the rotting vegetation in desperate times, but most people would rather starve.

Whereas most of the "alien" animals of the Rim are heavily genetically modified versions of Earth animals, the Mime is an absolute violation of all ethical principles: a ravenous, animalistic being created by genetically modifying humans.

Mimes are psionically gifted parasites, using their mental powers to disguise themselves as normal humans, infiltrating a human community and living among its members for weeks, months or even years. Their voracious appetites, however, cause them to constantly consume the easily available food provided by a stable colony. Only when food runs out will they resort to directly attacking their unwitting hosts.

Often seen foraging in groups among the undergrowth, they have gathered renown for their fiercely protective behavior over other members of their brood. Once provoked, the resulting rampage is the last thing many colonies see before their destruction under the might of an enraged pack. Despite its infamous reputation, the beast is still hunted across the Rim, not only for their thick hide or ample supply of meat, but also by warrior societies as a rite of passage.

rows.desc:
The Agaripod is a subspecies of the Wildpod that has grown in the secluded environment of a Mycotic Jungle. Its body is covered by Agarilux mushrooms that seem to be in a state of symbiosis. The Agaripod is almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass without doing much damage, but very weak to fire. Interestingly, it reproduces asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

Although risky, the Agaripod can be hunted or farmed for decent amounts of edible raw agarilux, which can be eaten raw and lasts a bit more than regular fungus.

rows.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

This Aerofleet seems to have been affected by prolonged exposure to the gases emanating from an ocular forest, and red pustules and blisters are appearing in its exterior membrane. Its hydrogen seems to be in the process of being turned into an acidic gas of unknown origins.

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, Aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound, and potentially used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research (Biofuel refining, Batteries and Advanced Fabrication).

rows.label: deermoss
rows.desc:
Deermoss are large forest herbivores covered in dense fur and symbiotic moss. They move silently through old woodlands and, though generally peaceful, their heavy frames and imposing antlers make them dangerous when threatened.

Their coats host medicinal vegetal fibers that can be harvested by careful handlers. They also produce a green, bitter and nutritious milk, but raising Deermoss is expensive: their appetite is enormous, and an unprepared colony can lose entire food stores trying to keep them alive.

Their original purpose seems less tied to isolated seeds and more to plant biodiversity as a whole: mosses, microflora, useful fibers and symbiotic organisms carried on the body itself. Some outlived their creators, naturalized, and came to be seen by tribes as signs of ancient forests returning.

rows.desc:
An artificial insect from the old world, resembling a cockroach in appearance but reaching up to 2 meters in length as an adult. They are friendly companions in daily life. However, due to genetic modifications that removed combat-related genes, despite possessing mandibles capable of tearing through adult humans and sturdy exoskeletons, they show almost no aggressive tendencies and are unsuitable for combat.
Through special genetic editing, these giant insects can be trained to autonomously seek out and consume waste, converting it into shellac through their unique digestive systems. rows.label: metallovore
rows.desc:
Metallovores are repulsive creatures genetically modified to fill a very specific niche: eating metals. The writhing tentacles in the animal's mouth secrete an organic substance that is capable of quickly rusting and dissolving most common metals, turning them into small flakes that serve as sustenance for the metallovore. They prefer small chunks of metal, since they can be more easily digested, but they will resort to digging into rocks in search of new metal if they can find none available.

Presumably, they were created to get rid of scrap metal, but they are mostly found in the wild now.

rows.label: swarmling
rows.desc:
Human space colonization slowly disseminated the Old Earth genelines across the stars, with all kinds of terran animals being used to populate and terraform the strange new worlds. Some of these animals, however, were pests, hitching a ride inside spaceships and multiplying at the expense of humanity. Swarmlings were one of such pests. Historians of the Ordo Historia theorize that Swarmlings were one of humanity's first successful genetic engineering creations, bred to enrich the biosphere of Mars, until they hitched a ride aboard an interstellar-bound colony ship.

Swarmlings are not very dangerous on their own, but... they are never on their own. They are an asexual species with a weird reproduction cycle: once they attack another creature, they implant larvae on it, and they hatch once the creature has died.

rows.desc:
The Helixien Slug is a genetically modified strain of the Leopard Slug, intended as a fast corpse disposal aid. Aside from the obvious size alteration, the Helixien constantly secretes a foul-smelling, corrosive gas that produces an uncomfortable, itchy sensation in living beings. This gas is mostly harmless, unless it comes into contact with decaying organic matter: it greatly accelerates corpse rotting, liberating a black putrid liquid known as "purge fluid" or corpse bile. The helixien happily feeds on this liquid sludge, although it can also feed on other organic matter if needed.

The sight of a Helixien Slug is quite revolting, and watching one wallowing in a pile of human corpses is, to say the least, a deeply traumatizing experience.

Despite being quite slow in open terrain, an insectoid black queen is capable of creating new black swarmlings at a rapid pace, and should never be allowed to settle down.
