Practically an overgrown and intelligent pest capable of tunnelling underground, so not even a nuke could clear an infestation. And it truly would be an infestation, as it has a gestation period measured in days rather than weeks, with a single breeding pair capable of wiping out an entire agricultural planet.

A colossal hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Incredibly durable and fast breeding, this surprisingly small hybrid can work as a durable screening force. One of the weakest colossal hybrids in terms of attack power but very few can outlast its incredibly robust physique.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor. Burrow underground: Thrumborats can burrow underground to make them almost immune to damage for a short while.

If they could be further bred to cross mountains and oceans, they’d be almost perfect.

The combination of genes has turned this somewhat peaceful herbivore/dendrovore into a full carnivore, which makes it easier to support their large appetite. As an intelligent predator, it can move incredibly quickly for its size and its attacks are incredibly fierce. It also lays massive eggs that can feed entire families.

rows.label: mycoid colossus
rows.desc:
The Mycoid Colossus is a variant of the Overgrown colossus native to a mycotic jungle.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with fungi, with several mutant Agarilux mushrooms growing on its back. These fungi trap insects and seem to provide sustenance in a symbiotic relationship with the colossus. Weirdly enough, this colossus reproduces by sporulation, instead of being a viviparous creature, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

When tamed, the Mycoid Colossus can be periodically "trimmed" to obtain raw agarilux mushrooms.

Female rikknit had ovum sacs connected to their abdomens, which when removed via butchery were considered a delicacy. Harvested ovum sacs could also be processed into an addictive substance called ji rikknit. It is likely these creatures are escaped livestock that have since gone on to establish wild populations.

rows.label: ocular jelly
rows.desc:
The Rim is filled with creatures that might be the product of either accelerated evolution from terrestrial origins, or, more often, of ancient human genetic engineering gone awry. The ocular jelly, however, is so fundamentally weird that some scientists have speculated about a possible extradimensional origin. Or perhaps it is just some cruel, if elaborate, practical joke.

It seems to have some biological similarities with the Aerofleet, being filled with a buoyant gas, but its effects on terrestrial ecosystems are incredibly unusual: the creature releases clouds of a reddish gas that is harmless to animals. However, when flora is exposed to it, it mutates and turns into strange specimens that share 98% of its genome with the jelly. This flora is almost inedible, and its relationship with the ocular jelly remains as of yet unexplained. As a floating creature, Ocular Jellies ignore terrain movement costs. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

The red goo seem to thrive in the strangely bizarre environment of the ocular forest, nibbling on the aberrant vegetation and periodically cloning themselves. NOTE: due to gameplay constraints, red goo will only self-replicate until the map holds 15 creatures, because I don't want to fry your computers. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

rows.label: manalope
rows.desc:
A floating, ticking time bomb that produces extremely reactive chemicals instead of chemfuel. Arguably more of a complex chemical distillery than an animal, it's a scientific miracle that it doesn’t explode every time it coughs. Surprisingly effective in combat in ways the enemy would really have preferred not knowing.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Thanks to its sac filled with buoyant chemicals, this hybrid never touches the ground and simply floats from location to location. Ignores terrain penalty costs and traps, while also being able to set down explosive traps of its own.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. Set trap ability: once every 3 days the manalope can set up an explosive IED. Hovers over terrain, ignoring terrain costs, and doesn't trigger ANY traps.

rows.label: shock goat
rows.desc:
Shock goats are domesticated cattle, renowned for their capacity to store static electricity on their bony structures, and releasing it as a defensive measure. Interestingly enough, the shock goat has characteristics common to many other Rim species, such as three pairs of eyes, and characteristics typical of Earth goats, such as the horns. This points to the conclusion that shock goats are actually a fertile cross-bred of two different creatures, created in the past by some human colony, and released in the wild for unknown reason.

Whatever the mystery behind their origins, nowadays they are commonly seen in farming communities in several Rim worlds, because they produce decent amounts of milk.

rows.label: angel moth
rows.desc:
Angel moths are beautiful lepidopterans that undergo metamorphosis, similar to other more mundane moths. Angel moths are yet another example of a genetically engineered project of waste disposal being abandoned, and its subjects being released into the wild.

The larvae are quite timid and harmless, and they are content with munching on sparse vegetation. The adult form of the moth, however, is voracious, and it will mainly consume its favourite food: clothing –in particular wool clothes, but many other natural fibres–. If no clothes are present they'll grudgingly devour grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are quite unruly creatures.

Adult specimens produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile, though care must be taken to keep it out of other moths' reach, since they'll happily consume it too.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

"At Attin frogdogs" were sought for the companionship they offered and kept as domestic pets.

This creature is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The Black Hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created and added to the Hive to increase its lethality. rows.desc:
Raptorkhans are huge feathered terror birds, too fast for their size and intelligent enough to hunt in pairs. Without relying on flight, they dominate terrain through speed, strength and talons capable of tearing heavy protection.

Mated pairs are territorial, especially near nests and thick-shelled eggs. Their claws are valued by some cultures as material for ceremonial blades, but obtaining one usually means facing one of the most dangerous hunts on the frontier.

Perhaps Raptorkhans began as controlled predators, bred for arenas, hunting reserves or aggressive fauna containment. Today they are something else: ambush birds adapted to the wild, with no masters and no arena.

Redhounds are clever beasts, and their intelligence is known throughout the lands, as they are capable of following even the most complex of orders. With only a few sanctioned kennel-masters allowed to breed them, it makes them a rare sight outside of a noble court.

Legends speak of incredibly intelligent and fierce dragons, ruling over whole planets with their devastating fire breaths and incomprehensible power. On the last days of the Forsaken, they will rise again and darken the skies, when the day of judgement comes.

rows.desc:
This large arthropod seems to be a distant relative of the smaller Frostmite, sharing many similarities in its body plan, though none of their carrion eating habits. It is a creature adapted to extreme low temperatures, feeding on half inorganic vegetation present in the unnatural propane lakes. Its low metabolism makes it a very efficient creature, which allows it to survive in such environments.

It is generally peaceful, and produces a blueish liquid that can be used as a milk substitute, so they are considered a nice farm animal for cold climates. Also, Jedi love this milk.

Intelligent creatures with complex social relationships, mastodons can be trained to carry out the most complex of tasks. They live a long time, and are known to remember events and relationships from many decades before.

rows.label: Jungle Rancor
rows.desc: Jungle rancors were a colossal subspecies of the more common rancor that had evolved on the planet Felucia, but existed on other worlds through suspected "exotic egg sales" and poaching. This subspecies had extreme sexual dimorphism, with the males (referred to as "rancor bulls") being pale whitish grey, having 4 short facial-tusks used for display and an elongated tail for balance. The females were a regal shade of navy blue with webbed hands and had additional layers of thick almost testudine-like growths on their backs (presumably to help avoid predation as juveniles). It's believed this subspecies of rancor was able to grow too such colossal sizes due to it's consumption of the local "fungal trees" on their native Felucia, supplementing it's otherwise carnivorous diet in times of prey sparsity.

rows.label: angel moth larva
rows.desc:
Angel moths are beautiful lepidopterans that undergo metamorphosis, similar to other more mundane moths. Angel moths are yet another example of a genetically engineered project of waste disposal being abandoned, and its subjects being released into the wild.

The larvae are quite timid and harmless, and they are content with munching on sparse vegetation. The adult form of the moth, however, is voracious, and it will mainly consume its favourite food: clothing –in particular wool clothes, but many other natural fibres–. If no clothes are present they'll grudgingly devour grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are quite unruly creatures.

Adult specimens produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile, though care must be taken to keep it out of other moths' reach, since they'll happily consume it too.

rows.label: larval atispec
rows.desc:
Atispecs are strange semi-insectoid creatures that undergo a radical metamorphosis, similar to old terran butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are basically harmless: a medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and usually ends up as some predator's meal. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season, and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.

An adult Atispec, however, is an entirely different matter: huge, carnivorous and venomous. Adult Atispecs are flying predators with a voracious appetite, and quite intelligent. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult specimens, but it has been found that it is not quite cost-effective to grow them during their 2-year-long vulnerable phase as larvae.

rows.desc:
The radyak is a peaceful herbivore bred to thrive in high radiation environments. Its ruminant digestive tract is composed of six bionic stomachs, reinforced with a lead-lined biolattice designed to extract residual radioactive material from grass cells. This radioactive material is then deposited in crystal-like formations that pierce the hard skin of the creature. This crystals can be harvested periodically, and refined into uranium in a standard chemfuel refinery.

The technology behind creating such carefully engineered creatures is completely out of reach of most Rim societies, so a radyak is a valued acquisition indeed.

The creatures possessed large mouths and many sharp teeth that could chew through most materials, including grasses and weeds, though they were not strictly herbivores and were known to consume other organisms, even members of their own kind.

rows.desc:
Gnauts are large grazing animals, robust and social, reminiscent of ancient wildebeest and wild bovine stock. They live well in herds and fit naturally into open ecosystems, turning ordinary vegetation into meat, hide, bones and horns.

They provide no milk or wool, but make up for it through simplicity: domesticable animals useful to colonies that need a stable source of resources without relying on rare byproducts. A lone gnaut rarely frightens a prepared colony; a threatened herd can still cause losses.

They may have been created as ecological support megafauna, a species made less to inspire wonder and more to occupy grasslands, sustain predators and feed human settlements.

Their skin is hard, leathery and bumpy, marked by islets of darker coulouration. Their enormous throat sacs let them call mates and make threats that can be heard over many miles. Their tongues shoot out at bullet speed when pursuing prey, be it large flies or small animals, able to penetrate armour and deal serious injury. Their leather is as thick as a bears, whom they sometimes fight for ownership of damp caves. Their meat tastes so much like chicken that you really can't feel the difference at all! Unlike with normal frogs, these genetically engineered giants go through a full transformation cycle while still in eggs, and upon hatching a fully formed (albeit smaller) specimen will emerge.

 Not originally from this RimWorld, giant toads are the result of genetic engineering targeted at teraforming planets to rich agricultural swamps. How it got here is anyone's guess.

 Giant Toads are even stronger with Giddy Up 2 (by Owlchemist), and become faster and hardier when mounted!

rows.label: giant snaptoad
rows.desc:
An enormous, carnivorous amphibian reigning as swamplands' apex predator. The tooth-filled maw that earned giant snaptoad its moniker can easily crush bone, and unhinge to swallow smaller prey whole after a leaping ambush from between the reeds. Its dentition, unique among contemporary amphibians, leads to speculation among scholars about whether giant snaptoad is a true toad, or an unrelated amphibian that convergently developed toad-like traits.

Giant snaptoads practice a rare form of child rearing called gastric brooding: upon fertilization, the eggs are immediately swallowed by the female and stored in a special chamber in their stomach. There, the tadpoles can safely hatch and develop, regurgitated by their parent only once they have transformed into froglets. However, in rare cases, the practice is omitted, and the tadpoles are left to fend for themselves in marshy waters.

Barogoth secrete a thick oily liquid that can be collected and used as a medicinal ointment. While applied on the body, it increase one's recovery against diseases and physical traumas.

rows.label: chameleon yak
rows.desc:
The Chameleon Yak is a long-haired domesticated bovid that has evolved a fascinating survival mechanism involving camouflage, similar to the way a chameleon changes its skin colour in response to different stimuli. The Chameleon Yak takes this a step further, changing its very metabolism according to the environment it is inhabiting at the time.

Chameleon Yaks will change their temperature tolerance depending on their environment, and even produce different types of wool. This change occurs at the cellular level and is very fast, but doesn't harm the animal in the slightest.

rows.label: aminox
rows.desc:
Aminox are huge cold-climate herbivores descended from ancient muskox-like lineages. Their thick coats and natural endurance let them survive across tundras, frozen plains and regions where ordinary cattle would not last long.

The true value of the Aminox lies in its milk. Dense, nutritious and rich in unusual amino compounds, it sustains colonies in extreme environments and serves as the basis for more potent derivatives. Its properties are not fully understood, but they are too consistent to be mere biological chance.

Perhaps the Aminox was part of a glitterworld bioproject aimed at the industrial production of valuable biocompounds. If so, its milk may be less a simple animal product than the functional residue of a forgotten living industry.

Manka cat populations were present on numerous worlds in the Outer Rim Territories (including Kashyyyk) and some tribes have been observed domesticating these creatures as fearsome attack beasts.

rows.label: thunderbeast
rows.desc:
The thunderbeast is a swine-like mammal capable of generating large electric currents by way of a highly specialized nervous system that has the capacity to synchronize the activity of disc-shaped, electricity-producing cells packed into a specialized electric organ.

Though they were initially created to serve as a way to generate bio-electricity similarly to Tetra slugs, thunderbeasts have naturally evolved over the centuries making them extremely unstable. Thunderbeasts can release jolts of electricity at great distances, and they will negatively affect weather if they are slaughtered. Thankfully, predators usually give them a wide berth.

Sadly, the mining company that created the Ironhusk beetles didn't account for this, and several planets on the Rim are now a barren ecological disaster.

rows.label: Empress butterfly
rows.desc:
The Empress Butterfly originates from an extremely rare type of planet – a Paradise Glitterworld. These planets have reached an extreme level of technology, but their inhabitants are very psychically sensitive, using their technology to offset any impact they might have on the planet's ecosystem and thereby anima. The Empress Butterfly was engineered as the perfect pollinator, gathering pollen from genetically engineered plants that increase the fertility of the surrounding terrain and releasing it nearby.

Adult Empress Butterflies have strict dietary constraints, as they demand a very specific type of food: flowers from the plant known as pollen trumpet, a long-lived decorative plant that was created to be in symbiosis with the butterfly. If they can't find pollen trumpets nearby, they will grudgingly resort to eating other farm plants nearby, thereby negating their usefulness to the colony. A good supply of mature pollen trumpets will be needed unless you want the butterfly to absolutely annihilate your crops.

rows.desc:
The concept behind the creation of Skiphounds was conceptually simple: DNA from an Animus Vox spliced into the genome of loyal companion dogs to create a creature that could always come when called, being capable of psionically detecting the wishes of its master. The result, however, was completely unexpected: Skiphounds uncontrollably use their latent psionic powers to "blink" in and out of existence, making them extremely unpredictable.

Skiphounds will use this psionic power constantly, unless eating or sleeping. An attacking Skiphound will rapidly teleport close to its prey, rendering a lot of defenses such as barricades and walls completely useless.

rows.desc: Naturally so hideous and maligned for its looks that it makes people flinch and cringe on sight, it is not often kept as a farm animal. For those that do so however, it produces milk of a high quality not seen elsewhere.
rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: red-horned larpah
rows.desc:
An elusive and deceitful creature, the red-horned larpah is a large leporidae with tall brown antlers protruding from it's head. While it may look gentle, larpah's apperence belies its predatory, fierce nature. As they grow older, a thick layer of dried blood from past battles coats their horns, earning them the moniker of "red-horned".

Deadly and tough for its size, its aggressiveness rarely discourages hunters from trying their luck at slaying the beast for its durable pelt and valuable antlers, which can be turned into a powerful mixture.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: terramorph
rows.desc:
This strange looking crustacean was created with a single goal in mind: mineral processing. The Terramorph can feed on iron compounds, and process them chemically to slowly turn them into a hardened mineral usually know as "sky steel", that is normally only found in asteroids.

The transmutation process is very slow, so the Terramorph needs to spend quite a lot of time surrounded by mined Steel lumps. The Terramorph can also slowly consume, but not convert, steel slag chunks.

specials.text: eats something no normal animal eats

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: bearcat
rows.desc:
Massive, fluffy murder babies is just one of the many “cute” nicknames made for this animal, their only downside being that they’re unable to purr. Because they’re so large, they often end up knocking over the people they’re trying to show affection to before laying on top of them for warmth.

An ursine hybrid with recessive feline genes. Retaining their intelligence and being faster and more fierce in combat, they are adorable killing machines that love to nuzzle. They prefer easier prey and can be slaughtered for a valuable pelt, you monster.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All primary bear hybrids have stun attacks. Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability and a short nuzzle period. The pelt can be sold or used in the art workbench to create rugs.

rows.label: colossal aerofleet
rows.desc:
A huge, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path. One of the few rare creatures around here that strangely isn’t out for human blood. Well, isn’t that nice?

This Aerofleet has somehow grown to extreme size. A small number of younger Aerofleets seem to be attracted to it and follow it everywhere.

Colossal Aerofleets produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as Blue Gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound, and potentially used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research (Biofuel refining, Batteries and Advanced Fabrication).

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.label: thrumbocat
rows.desc:
The other half of the super predator duo, along with the Thrumwolf, exchanging some ferocity and durability in exchange for going for the trachea and spitting suffocating hairballs. That might not sound that dangerous but imagine having a fistful of hair pulled from a shower drain smothering your mouth, and you’ll realise that’s still not disgusting enough. But for those that it appreciates, it will often pin them down and snuggle them given the chance.

A colossal hybrid with recessive feline genes. A large predator with an insane appetite with a focus on ferocious attacks that restrict their prey’s breathing. Extremely agile with a soft spot for those it loves, best suited for biomes that support enough wildlife to sate its hunger.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor.

rows.label: spiderhorse
rows.desc:
Arachnophobia is no joke for many people, and the researcher that created this armoured arachnid had an inherent desire to share their fear with others. Granted they passed out, frothing at the mouth, when the creature emerged from the pod, but damn it it’s hard to argue with results in a riding companion that can not only keep up with the competition, but also disable them and eat them on the go as a tasty snack.

An equine hybrid with recessive insectoid genes. A rather slow and filthy hybrid of this category, but it works very well as a ride due to the multiple legs easing the burden of long distance travel inherent to caravaning. However, their main advantage is that they are also incredibly capable in combat, being armour plated and capable of both high damage and ranged stunning attacks by shooting globs of sticky threads.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM.

rows.label: great devourer
rows.desc:
Great Devourers are armoured worms known for their unquenchable appetite. Once a Great Devourer arrives, it will proceed to gorge itself on small prey, and total ecosystem collapse is almost a certainty.

Luckily, they won't attack large creatures, including humans, unless provoked. Their whole name is in fact a pun, since they are not very resilient and are easily dispatched. They have however slow regenerative capabilities.

Aiwhas are sometimes sold so as to be used as mounts on worlds that have a breathable atmosphere, and could be used for performing reconnaissance, or to traverse between two outposts without any concern for the trail or terrain.

rows.label: bearscarab
rows.desc:
An absolute unit of an insectoid hybrid, this massive chubster is incredibly smart and hard to kill. All the excess blubber has been replaced with either chitin or muscle fibre, so don’t go making comments about their bulk.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Very thick armour plating and a calm temperament make this hybrid an excellent combat animal. Requires little in the way of retraining and can dish out respectable damage as well.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

rows.label: bearhorse
rows.desc:
While they’re surprisingly tireless when they have a home to rest at, these manned mares are quite reluctant to hurry along when made to carry loads in a caravan. Their body’s efficiency means they’ll get a task done when it needs to, and not a moment sooner. What makes it worse is that they’re smart enough to know that they’re cute - and powerful - enough to get away with it.

An equine hybrid with recessive ursine genes. The inherent hibernating nature of bears has combined with the high energy of horses to create this particular hybrid that requires little in the way of rest and a much more efficient and versatile digestive system. They are quite a bit slower as a consequence, along with their higher body mass.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM.

rows.label: atispec
rows.desc:
Atispecs are strange semi-insectoid creatures that undergo a radical metamorphosis, similar to old terran butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are basically harmless: a medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and usually ends up as some predator's meal. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season, and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.

An adult Atispec, however, is an entirely different matter: huge, carnivorous and venomous. Adult Atispecs are flying predators with a voracious appetite, and quite intelligent. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult specimens, but it has been found that it is not quite cost-effective to grow them during their 2-year-long vulnerable phase as larvae.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/). 

Based on a design by Brent Hollowell: https://www.artstation.com/brenthollowell

rows.desc:
This hairy omnivore is descended from escaped pigs and evolved for living in the wild.

Its tusks make it a better fighter than its domesticated pig cousins. Unfortunately, it is too unruly to be trained in the most complex tasks.

rows.desc: Engineered for chemicals production, the boomalope grows a large sac of volatile chemicals on its back. Though it is weak and fragile for its size, other animals have learned to avoid it because of the huge explosion it produces when it dies. It can be milked to produce chemfuel - very carefully.

rows.label: overgrown colossus
rows.desc:
The Overgrown Colossus is a very strange beast. This gargantuan beast is one of the few creatures in the Rim that wasn't directly created by man's scientific curiosity, arising naturally in some remote swamp-filled planet, albeit from some original forgotten terran creature.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with vegetation, with several small trees growing on its back. These trees do photosynthesis and help provide nutrients for the Colossus.

When tamed, the Overgrown Colossus can be periodically "trimmed" to obtain wood.

Based on concept art by Arvalis: https://www.deviantart.com/arvalis/art/Overgrown-Colossus-Concept-Art-144699628

rows.label: phoenix owlcat
rows.desc:
A genetically modified feline with avian characteristics, the Phoenix Owlcat was created as a durable alternative to fragile baseline cats. A loyal companion that isn't so easily hunted and slaughtered by the hostile lifeforms present on the planets of the Rim.

The ancient popular folklore of cats having nine lives was used as a pattern to create the Phoenix Owlcat: a swarm of powerful mechanites in its bloodstream is capable of saving it from up to 9 lethal wounds before being lost to decoherence.

RW animal graphic inspired by original creation by RobtheDoodler (check his Deviant Art page at https://www.deviantart.com/robthedoodler!).

rows.desc:
A small burrowing mammal with glistening silver fur. Elusive and skittish, the silver mole can rarely be seen outside the safety of its underground den deep in the mountains.

Many woodsmen make a habit of patrolling silver mole habitats, hoping to catch the critter while it digs for its favourite food - white truffles, rare mushrooms with sublime taste that grows under stony soils.

rows.desc:
You wouldn’t think something so small could eat so much, but that’s the price you pay for the sake of convenience. That convenience is sporadic, low in nutrition and very thin, an effect commonly described as “nerfing”.

An avian hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Loves to wander so it must be securely penned, but they make for a surprising pack beast. Capable of producing the holy trinity of milk, eggs and wool, however they can be quite lacking in substance.

rows.label: mecha-rat
rows.desc:
This tiny cybernetic organism can be mass-produced as a kind of "suicide weapon". It is very fast, and armed with a short ranged stun gun, so hordes of mecha-rats can be sent to the front lines to keep enemies stunned and in check. 

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color>Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, allowing the colonists to send the mecha-rat to the front lines to quickly stun enemies. Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

rows.label: catman

Despite being a health violation, they were extremely popular with the infirms as they not only fed patients but also engaged in conversation and gave friendly headbutts. It is also alleged that their purring helped broken bones heal quicker, but no conclusive evidence has been shown.

This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. Catmen are compassionate animals that will help with feeding medical patients around the colony.

This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. The mansquirrel is a nocturnal animal that sleeps during the day. Will obey orders to clear snow around the colony.

Their long elegant wings are vestigial and primarly serve in the mating season, in order to attract new partners or to scare off predators by appearing bigger than they are.

Some hunters have taken a liking to owlcats for their ability to quickly track and hunt rodents.

This creates a stacking effect of boosting the amount of food foraged for every other catffalo in the trip. They’re quite hardy too but should be kept away from combat.

rows.desc:
- "O, His Excellency, Most High Royal Geneticist: I have laboured hard to complete your latest assignment, and it pleases me to say that I finally have results to show you."

- "Excellent, and just in time. The King is eagerly awaiting this specimen  for his menagerie. Show me."

- "Lo and behold! A magical creature most astounding!"

- "What the HELL is that!?

- "Uh... it's... uh... the creature you... requested... uh, Sir."

- "You drooling moron! I said a FLAMING PHOENIX!"



The Flamingo Phoenix is a failed genetic creation that will erupt in a flaming conflagration when it dies, leaving a fire-resistant egg behind. This egg will soon hatch into a new specimen. The only way to get rid of a Flamingo Phoenix is to destroy these eggs before they hatch. Sometimes two eggs will be produced, this being the only viable way of reproduction the species has.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

All backstories have the same result - an adorable, intelligent furry quadruped who makes a great companion on lonely rimworlds.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can morph into various specialized castes.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All canine hybrids get the Adrenaline rush ability, which allows them to move at 200% speed for a short time, but be tired and move slower for half a day afterwards. Blood frenzy ability: after killing prey, the wolfchicken receives 200% speed for an hour.

These flatworms can grow accustomed to people, and have even been genetically modified to nuzzle, and their odd squishy texture is surprisingly nice to pet. Though their brains are so small, it is doubtful they gain anything from nuzzling.

rows.label: crystalline caracal
rows.desc:
A heavily modified medium-sized wild cat, the crystalline caracal can often be seen lazying around in the sun, recharging its internal energies. It can later use this stored energy to release a powerful blast of concentrated light. Typically nocturnal, the crystalline caracal is highly secretive and difficult to observe. It is territorial, and lives mainly alone or in pairs.

Contrary to other purely photosynthetic creatures, the caracal can also hunt small prey, and it needs both kinds of sustenance to survive.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

A surprisingly clean animal dubbed the “owl-bear” by those that find them amusing as they attempt to fly by rapidly flapping their stubby vestigial wings. That is until they get their eyes pecked out and flattened by their weight.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All primary bear hybrids have stun attacks. Although too heavy to fly, it can use its wings to nullify terrain movement costs.

They had a vicious bark and bite, which meant they could be quite effective for protection.

Some insane madman thought it would be an excellent idea to strap a flamethrower to a dog and send it out into the world to see what happens. Don’t be surprised to find out this unusual hybrid started a massive forest fire trying to hunt a rabbit.

A bit more dim-witted compared to their baseline, due to a large amount of brain processing power dedicated to the complex internal organs that permit it to spit out burning chemfuel. Excellent flankers thanks to their increased speed and ranged ability.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All canine hybrids get the Adrenaline rush ability, which allows them to move at 200% speed for a short time, but be tired and move slower for half a day afterwards.

With its reduced durability, the Artilleron can't withstand intense battles and is often deployed in the rear lines to eliminate high priority targets and secure strategic objectives from afar. It can also swap weapons between its mortar and a low damage, high accuracy micro needle gun to avoid causing friendly fire with its explosives.

rows.desc: An advanced combat mechanoid designed to excel in high-risk combat situations. With a height of around 5 feet, it is armed with a rapid-firing tactical mechanoid shotgun. Unlike its predecessor, the Militor, the Bellicor is highly durable and has the ability to withstand intense battles. It is often deployed in the front lines to eliminate high priority targets and secure strategic objectives. Due to its advanced capabilities, the Bellicor is more expensive to produce and maintain, but is still highly valued by those who seek to dominate the battlefield.

rows.label: apoptosis
rows.desc:
Malice incarnate, the Apoptosis is an advanced Apocriton that acts as a commander designed to coordinate and motivate other mechs during long extermination campaigns. They are less adept at resurrecting other mechanoids than Apocritons, but the aura of hate they emanate is so powerful and intense that it will cause uncontrollable despair on those too close to it.

The Apoptosis is armed with two dangerous ranged weapons: an acid spewer that can melt the flesh out of the bone, and a psychically charged energy pulse that can damage the very soul of its target.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> The Apoptosis is a stronger version of the Apocriton, and should be treated as such. Its hatred aura will make everyone nearby scream in despair. It will unleash two devastating ranged attacks against defenders, as well as resurrect nearby mechanoids, although not as often as an Apocriton would.

They also have the ability to regenerate their wounds with fast acting mechanites.

Regeneration is 0.1 damage to a random wound every 10 ticks, 1/6th of a second.

If toggled to not spawn via mod options, they will get replaced by a Scyther.

They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. Objectively cute when you give them a good brushing, but have a nasty habit of overshooting hand-fed snacks and biting on hands due to poor eyesight. A saddle is recommended for riding, as there is little fat and no fur to cushion their boney structure and loose skin.

A perfect canine animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon can be slaughtered for a valuable pelt, which can either be used for decoration or sold.

A canine hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Stronger, more aggressive and with a bigger appetite, this hybrid’s particular lethality comes from its tendency to attack the enemy’s head to try and decapitate them.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All canine hybrids get the Adrenaline rush ability, which allows them to move at 200% speed for a short time, but be tired and move slower for half a day afterwards. Dogs and cats are domesticated predators who are just the absolute cutest. So someone wanted to see how dangerous they could make something by combining these two proto predators. The results could be imagined but we’ll let them speak for themselves.

A canine hybrid with recessive feline genes. A combination of two predators makes for an incredible loyal killing machine. Quick, lethal, low maintenance and a desire for companionship. If that wasn’t already enough, it can even randomly attack twice by lunging with both claws and teeth.

A reptile hybrid with recessive canine genes. Fast, intelligent and with a nasty venomous bite, these hybrids make for an excellent hunting hound. They lack any notion of fear so they may end up going after much larger, more dangerous prey and achieving a pyrrhic victory.

Its most obvious power is its ability to resurrect recently-killed mechs by supercharging their self-repair processes. Less obviously, it is intelligent and psychically present, radiating hatred into the minds of anyone in a wide radius. It can also move quickly with its built-in jump launcher.

While all mechanoids have a dim psychically-present intelligence, only the apocriton and a few others truly feel hatred for their victims and understand the suffering they inflict.

Despite its unusual appearance, the wastedeer is a graceful and nimble creature, easily navigating the treacherous terrain of the wasteland. Though it may not pose a direct threat, its presence serves as a reminder of the dangers of a world overrun by pollution.

rows.desc:
A basic reusable transport pod, the Frog is a relatively cheap vehicle that is the first option when it comes to flying without crashing into the ground. Several times faster than conventional transport pods with acceptable armour for its single passenger, making it an ideal ambush vehicle.

Even worse than other tier 1 vehicles, fuel efficiency isn’t a thing with this transportation. Care must be taken to either refuel at the landing site or travel with enough spare fuel to make the trip back.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when on the move.

A squad and mortar deployment pod, the Toad is a somewhat expensive vehicle to quickly mount a siege on a nearby locale without exposing your gunners to danger. With more armour than a tank and a design made to be deployed from orbit, it makes for a semi-disposable assault vehicle.

Fuel efficiency is not the design of this vehicle, consider only deploying on short distances with enough fuel to make it back.

rows.desc:
A watercraft featuring a lateral support float known as an outrigger, which is fastened to one of the sides of the main hull. An outrigger generates stability as a result of the distance between its hulls rather than due to the shape of each individual hull. As such, the hulls of outrigger boats are typically longer, narrower and more hydrodynamically efficient.

rows.label: termite
rows.desc: A medium-sized mechanoid. Termites specialize in burrowing, digging, and breaking through defensive structures. Defenders need to decide whether to try to eliminate the termite before it can dig through their defenses, or take it where it emerges.

rows.label: toxlion
rows.desc:
The toxlion is a sad reflection of what once was a proud and powerful predator. Its toxic environment has left it weak and emaciated, forcing it to survive by feeding on waste. Despite its diminished state, the Toxlion is still a threat. Its bites and claws have a high chance of spreading the toxflu, and it hunts in large packs to make up for its lack of strength and speed.

Toxflu is a highly contagious and rapidly striking disease, characterized by fever, cough, fatigue, and difficulty breathing. It spreads quickly through contact with infected bodily fluids. Those who contract Toxflu can experience severe respiratory distress and, in severe cases, death. It goes away nearly as quickly as it appears, however anyone who interacted socially with a person suffering from toxflu has a chance of catching it.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses, animal products; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: phalanx
rows.desc:
A hulking mechanoid based on a rhinoceros beetle body plan. The phalanx's plasteel carapace hides a very powerful cryogenic engine capable of constantly producing compacted pellets of supercooled gas. These are fired from an aperture at the mechanoid's head.

This cryo-weapon has a very low range, but it can be very dangerous for beings susceptible to frostbite.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Will explode on death with 10 Frostbite damage on a 2.9 tile radius.

If toggled to not spawn via mod options, they will get replaced by a Pikeman.

rows.label: Simbakub
rows.desc:
Simbakubs are large primitive lions, dangerous not only for their strength but for the way they hunt in packs. Across savannas, deserts and other harsh biomes, they stalk gnauts, direhorses and travelers, closing in silently before attacking as a group.

Wounding a single Simbakub can pull the entire pack into the fight. This collective response becomes even more dangerous in the presence of an Alpha, which keeps the hunt coordinated and turns already aggressive animals into a disciplined force. Taming them is difficult, but tribes and colonies that succeed gain fierce, loyal guardians capable of inspiring courage in nearby allies.

Perhaps they were shaped to restore predatory pressure in open ecosystems, keeping large herbivores moving and preventing overpopulation. On the modern frontier, that ecological function has become something else: packs intelligent enough to turn hunting into ambush.

Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Giant beavers, the largest to ever exist.
Its incisors aren't as well fitted for cutting wood as those of its modern equivalents, which is why it doesn't bother with constructing dams. This makes it so it will more often have to resort to either running from predators or attempting to fight them off, instead of simply hiding away from them.

rows.desc:
A huge mechanical worm armed with a dangerous chemfuel flamethrower. Their weapon has a very short range, so don't let a fireworm approach your defenses!

The fireworm superficially resembles a Frostbound Behemoth. A coincidence? Or perhaps mechanoids take living things as a blueprint for their units. If so, you wouldn't want to see what a biological scyther looks like...

A muffalo hybrid with recessive avian genes. A bit too slow and weak for a caravan companion but it makes  for a vicious and suicidal protective companion. Produces a thick, chunky milk that tastes like a protein shake.

rows.desc:
An incredible, large fur baby that not only wants you to scratch its belly, but regularly and without fear of getting your eyes gouged out by their massive claws. Also they’re smart enough to go after prey less than half their size, but that’s more so they don’t have to spend so much time grooming themselves afterwards.

A perfect feline animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon is incredibly intelligent and can be properly trained with minimal retraining, as well as being an excellent and affectionate companion.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability and a short nuzzle period. Cat reflexes ability: twice per day, it can use an ability that gives it further melee capabilities.

rows.desc:
Combining fierce independence with an animal suited for travelling long distances might not have been the best idea. But critics have clearly never been nuzzled by a giant cat only to be buried alive in a pile of insulating hair in the winter, so what do they know.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive feline genes. Not the best for caravan duty but their regular grooming produces bundles of thick wool and can be milked for a rather disgusting milk filled with hair. A low maintenance way of getting more hair than you bargained for.

rows.label: frost lynx
rows.desc:
A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the Frost lynx shares its genetic template with the Genix, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.

The Frost lynx was modified with hydrofluorocarbon-laced hemoglobin in its blood, allowing it to survive in extremely low temperatures, with a core body heat that would normally kill most creatures. As such, it is capable of using its low body heat to cause frostbite wounds in its victims, quickly incapacitating them. If it feels threatened, it can produce a ranged spit projectile containing particles of its blood, which explodes on impact and coves an area in dangerous freezing crystals.

rows.label: genix
rows.desc:
A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the Genix shares its genetic template with the Frost lynx, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.

Whereas the Frost lynx is perfectly adapted to cold temperatures, the Genix is usually found on milder climates, as it has a complex biological refrigeration system that allows it to decrease ambient temperature wherever it goes. If domesticated, this strange ability could perhaps be used to refrigerate an enclosed space. However, the Genix has a tendency to explode if it receives too much damage, making it a quite fragile creature.

rows.desc:
An automated, mobile mechanoid factory. The assembler is designed for efficient energy-to-matter conversion. Using its advanced molecular assembly system, it can convert various forms of energy into usable materials with remarkable precision. This particular assembler doesn't need to consume organic matter to aid in the conversion, being compatible with standard mech rechargers.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> At random, the Assembler will produce 10: Steel, Gold, Uranium, Plasteel, Silver, Go-Juice, Flake, Yayo, Chocolate, Synthread, Cloth, Jade, Devilstrand cloth, Muffalo wool, Heavy leather, Explosive shells, Industrial medicine, Neutroamine, Chemfuel or Components every 24 hours.

rows.label: pristine slurrypede
rows.desc: Although rare, mechanoids have been known to capture prisoners, and the Slurrypede is their solution to feed them in the most efficient way possible. The Slurrypede is a modified bio-mechanoid capable of extracting energy from standard mech rechargers and use it to process inorganic matter into a homogeneous organic slurry. This slurry is edible for carnivore and omnivore animals, but barely, and completely indigestible for herbivores.

rows.label: dewback chariot
rows.desc:
One dewback, a yoke, and a light two-wheeled platform to stand on. It is the fastest thing a scavenger clan can build out of scrap, and it is fast only where the ground is already flat and packed.

Dewbacks are big grey-green lizards that do not hurry and do not need to. They drink at dawn, walk through the worst of the heat without complaint, and will keep a steady pace long after a warm-blooded animal has lain down in whatever shade it can find.

Off a road the chariot is close to useless — the wheels are narrow, they cut into soft sand, and the rider spends more time hauling it free than riding it.

rows.label: eopie sled
rows.desc:
Two eopies in harness, and a flatbed of lashed scrap riding on runners because wheels drown in soft sand.

They are patient, sour-smelling animals with long necks and a hide like cracked leather, and they will walk all day on almost nothing. Water they need. Food they mostly find, chewing whatever grey thing is rooted between the rocks. They complain constantly through their snouts, they spit when handled badly, and they are worth every bit of it — an eopie team will cross open pan in the heat of the day and be ready to do it again after a night's rest and a trough.

The sled is the point. Runners spread the load where a cart would dig in, so you can haul a wreck's worth of salvage back across the flats instead of picking through it for what fits in a pack.

rows.desc:
Inherently less effective at refining chemfuel when allowed to rest at its leisure while also being a good pack animal and riding companion. During distant travels, the long periods of engagement for their muscles actively puts their glands into overdrive. Quite effective should there be a vehicle that uses chemfuel, but don’t ask how that would work out. Maybe it’s the desire to compete against machinery or knowing that if the vehicle breaks down it's gonna have to do all that bloody walking again.

An equine hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. While they are comparatively slower, their inherent need to exercise means that their capability in producing chemfuel is severely hampered if their muscles aren’t engaged for long periods of time. When travelling as part of a caravan, their chemfuel production speed is effectively quadrupled.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM.

This ferocious feline is ready to tear up the track and hunt prey comically smaller than itself. They’re also incredibly smart and have a tendency to stalk their owners when their backs are turned. Don’t worry though, it only wants to pin you down and drown you in fur and saliva.

They are only slightly less effective as horses in riding but have better stamina, in exchange they are pure carnivores so their diet can be rather restrictive.

Always starts as draftable, even if not using a controller booster to create it. Pounce ability: when drafted, the player can use the pounce ability to make the hybrid jump around. The ability can be triggered every 2 hours.

Dude, this shit is the shit, where did you get this, man?” - Recording playback used in a hearing against a disgraced genetic scientist for misappropriating government funding.

rows.label: manehound
rows.desc:
Manehounds are large feral guardian dogs descended from ancient cold-climate shepherd breeds. Their dense coats, heavy neck manes and watchful posture still reveal an animal made to stand between the herd and the threat.

Generations in the wild made them cautious and territorial, but never fully erased their domestic instincts. Unlike wolves or true hunting predators, Manehounds watch, endure and hold position. Once tamed, a Manehound can become a loyal guardian of pens, sleeping quarters and vulnerable colonists.

Perhaps they were only working dogs carried too far by selection, climate and abandonment. Today they occupy a rare space between beast and companion: wild enough to survive alone, close enough to humanity to return.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: fungus, meat, corpses, animal products, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: thrumwolf
rows.desc:
There’s a saying about the scientific community, namely “your scientists were so preoccupied with whether they could, they didn’t stop to think if they should”. This is entirely relevant to this creature, a super predator with practically no equal, a single one of these is enough to require an entire rainforest to support their daily sustenance. If that wasn’t bad enough, they were made along with the Thrumbocat as part of a duo.

A colossal hybrid with recessive canine genes. A large predator with an insane appetite with the necessary ferocity to support itself, very few colonies can support the diet of such a hybrid. Incredibly robust, fast and a terrifying ferocity, they will hunt multiple times a day and often go after prey much bigger than themselves.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor.

rows.label: direhorse
rows.desc:
Direhorses are colossal ancestral horses covered in dense coats that protect them across frozen plains and harsh open country. Their herds move over great distances at a steady pace, keeping strength and endurance where lesser mounts would quickly wear down.

Once domesticated, a Direhorse becomes one of the most valuable caravan mounts on the frontier, combining speed, carrying capacity and battlefield presence. Even so, its size and strength make any hunt or taming attempt a real risk for unprepared colonists.

Perhaps the lineage was preserved or reconstructed for transport on cold, underdeveloped worlds. This is not an elegant stable creature; it is a mount made to cross bad ages.

rows.label: Simbakub Alpha
rows.desc:
Simbakub Alphas are rare and immense individuals, strong enough to roam alone until they find or claim a new pack. Their roars mark wide territories, and few smaller predators remain nearby once an Alpha begins to hunt.

When accepted by a pack, the Alpha becomes leader, protector and center of the collective response. Its presence reinforces the discipline of nearby Simbakubs, making coordinated attacks more dangerous and making the group harder to break in combat. Alphas reproduce only with other Alphas, keeping their lineage separate from the rest of the species.

The Alpha seems less like a simple size variation and more like a rare biological function: a living command point for packs built around cooperation, territory and survival. Where it passes, the ecosystem learns to make room.

This particular humanoid has undergone some mental evolution while at the same time suffering from physical devolution, resembling more closely humanity’s distant evolutionary ancestors. Just don’t say monkey.

A perfect humanoid animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon can drive man’s curiosity ever forward by providing a boost to research speed with a well-placed insightful word of wisdom.

rows.label: ronto wagon
rows.desc:
Two rontos in front of a four-wheeled wagon with a hide roof stretched over hoops. The roof is not comfort. It is the difference between arriving and arriving with heatstroke.

Rontos are enormous, dun-coloured and profoundly nervous. They will carry a house across open pan all day and then bolt at a shadow, so the harness is built to come apart faster than it goes on, and nobody sensible sleeps under the wheels.

Leather strapping under the bed takes the worst of the ruts out. Three can ride in the back without arriving bruised, which on a two-day crossing is worth more than speed.

The dewbacks are the reason it works. They are slow to start and impossible to stop, they do not spook at noise the way a ronto does, and they will walk straight at something that is shooting back — which is a rarer quality in a draft animal than it sounds.

It is not cavalry. It is a way to put a shooter somewhere they could not have walked to, and to get them out again afterwards.

Their feathers contain rare oils used to craft elixirs that sharpen the senses. Taming a Harpeagle is possible, but requires skill, courage and a constant food supply; keeping a predator this size alive can cost as much as capturing it.

If they were ever shaped for surveillance, hunting or aerial control of fauna, that purpose has been lost. What remains is a territorial lineage, intelligent enough to recognize threats and strong enough to turn a nest into forbidden ground.

This leads to toxic buildup and cancerous growths that must be swiftly removed before they spread, making the Toxscorpion one of the most dangerous creatures in the wasteland.

rows.label: Capryak
rows.desc:
Capryaks are megagoats of the cold regions, adapted to tundras, frostbitten forests and mountainous terrain. Their dense coats, thick hides and long horns make them resistant to cold and difficult to bring down, especially when wounded.

Colonies can raise them for rugged wool, harsh but nourishing milk, and horns strong enough for primitive weapons. The problem is keeping them: because of their size, appetite and stubborn temperament, a Capryak demands more food and handling than common livestock.

Perhaps they descend from mountain lineages altered to survive where traditional herds would fail. They do not seem refined; they seem made to endure.

rows.desc:

Although usually docile when kept in herds, duskhorns can become dangerous when wounded or when one of their own is threatened. Hunting them without preparation can turn a valuable source of milk, wool, meat and horns into a fight that is hard to control.

The species seems to have been shaped to survive extreme climates and support isolated communities. Among tribes, they still carry a reputation for good fortune; to more practical colonists, they are one of the most useful ways to turn harsh pasture into rare resources.

rows.desc:
Scarodons are solitary apex predators marked by saber-like fangs, robust bodies and thick fur covered in old scars. Roaming boreal and temperate forests, they are strong enough to hunt megafauna and dangerous enough to make even armed colonists hesitate.

Although they eat almost anything, Scarodons seem to prefer large and valuable prey. Bringing one down can yield rare resources, including the Ember Heart, an unstable organ associated with extreme heat, aggressive regeneration and bursts of force during combat.

It is hard to say whether the Scarodon began as animal, weapon or mistake. Its body carries signs of a lineage made to clear territories, survive without command and keep hunting long after its creators disappeared.

Some argue that this is the ideal form of muffalo for nomad tribes, as they produce everything they need to survive winters and are large enough to feed said tribe through the harshest of seasons.

Very unusual in that it doesn’t help a caravan speed along, largely due to it excessively foraging and eating various vegetation from new locations, as well as roughage to help with digestion. The benefit from this behaviour is that this stimulation is the only way it’ll produce milk and wool, so herds of these hybrids can be taken on a long journey to provide produce vital to small and starting colonies.

rows.label: furpotamus
rows.desc:
Furpotamus are colossal, fur-covered ancestors of modern hippos, adapted to wetlands, swamps and cold riverbanks. Despite their heavy bodies, they move easily through flooded terrain and become far more dangerous near water.

They are herbivores, but territorial when harmed or pressured. Domestication is possible, though difficult due to their size, appetite and grazing needs. Hunters seek them for dense fat, heavy bones, resilient hide and thick fur, but a cornered Furpotamus can crush a poorly positioned team.

Perhaps the species was bio-engineered as part of living water-filtration systems on polluted rimworlds. Without genetic maintenance, many herds returned to a semi-wild state, turning old ecological instruments into swamp threats.

rows.label: Plastemmoth
rows.desc:
Plastemmoths are colossal biometallic beasts that roam frozen and temperate regions. Their strength, resilience and body mass make them one of the most dangerous hunts on the frontier, especially when encountered moving with other members of the herd.

Over a lifetime, plastite formations slowly grow within the body, shaped by biological processes and extreme environmental pressure. These unstable crystals are valuable because they can be refined with industrial steel to produce plasteel, turning each carcass into a mixture of prize, risk and logistical disaster.

Perhaps the Plastemmoth was an attempt to turn entire ecosystems into slow factories of strategic material. Today, however, it is less a living machine than a migrating mountain carrying mineral wealth inside its bones.

rows.label: teramantis
rows.desc: An incredibly rare and monstrously large insectoid of the Chelis geneline, the teramantis is the formidable leader of insectoid hives on the steppe planets of Chelis. Known as a prime male, this massive insectoid is equipped with lethal ripper claws sharp enough to cleave armored vehicles in two. Complementing its fearsome offensive capabilities, the teramantis boasts a large set of wings, granting it the ability to soar across the vast landscapes in pursuit of prey for hundreds of miles. Its aerial prowess and deadly strength make it a dreaded apex predator on Chelis, commanding respect and fear from all who dwell within its territory. Upon death, it’s possible to extract a Chelis pherocore from its body.

Demolishers are armed with a very dangerous short range turret that fires demolisher charges, capable of blowing up even the strongest walls in two or three hits. Once they have ruptured a colony's outer defenses, their enormous plasteel reinforced claws can make short work of anyone foolish enough to stay in their way.

These singularities are generated by a complex fusion reactor at the heart of the machine, which channels and amplifies energy from nearby stars via microscopic skipgates. When fired, the singularities unleash devastating amounts of energy, capable of obliterating entire structures in a single blast, as well as creating secondary energy discharges that arc to nearby targets. The Starfire is heavily armored and equipped with advanced targeting systems, allowing it to rain destruction from afar. However, due to the intense energy requirements of the singularities, the Starfire is only deployed in the most extreme situations, where its destructive power is needed to turn the tide of battle.

A bantha is a mountain of shaggy hide under a pair of spiral horns, and it is stupid in the specific way that makes an animal useful — it will lean into a load until the load moves or the harness breaks, and it does not form an opinion about which. They eat anything with roots, they carry their own water for days, and the Tuskens have built an entire way of living on them for good reason.

Use it for salvage: hull plate, machinery, whatever came out of a wreck too heavy to carry. It is slow, it is terrible off a road, and it will still be doing this long after the fast things have shaken themselves apart.

Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

And we’re here to tell you it doesn’t exist. But we’ve gotten close in that this one will typically harvest your plants before it eats them for worse nutritional gain. Unless it’s trees, in which case we got nothing.

A colossal hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Considerably easier to train and maintain, this particular hybrid will help around the colony by cutting and harvesting designated plants. Unusually lean for how much it eats, it won’t provide much in butchering.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor. Thrumbomen will obey orders to cut and harvest plants around the colony.

rows.desc: While a normal giant frog will rarely reach a 30 year lifespan, their gene code does allow 1 in 10000 to undergo a mutation that functionally stops their aging. Those toads will grow in size, power and appetite until one day earning the name of King Toad, a stoic mountain in the skin of an amphibian, swallowing its prey whole and leaving nothing behind. rows.label: dunbear
rows.desc:
Dunbears are ancient cave bears of monumental size, adapted to extreme cold and mountainous regions. They spend long periods in deep hibernation, waking with the thaw to roam the surface in search of food.

Hunting a Dunbear is a dangerous decision. Its mass, resilience and brute strength let it survive wounds that would drop most predators, while its dense and valuable fur makes it a tempting prize for prepared colonies.

Perhaps they were created as containment predators, an old answer to terraformed ecosystems that slipped out of control. Today, however, they guard nothing. They are only hungry survivors of a project that forgot to die.

specials.text: predator — hunts other animals, and colonists count

rows.diet: meat, corpses; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: diabolus
rows.desc:
An ultra-heavy mechanoid with an ultra-powerful hellsphere cannon. Made for siegebreaking, its hellsphere cannon takes time to charge up a shot, but can melt concrete and vaporize bone. The diabolus dissipates the hellsphere cannon's waste power in a heat column mounted on its back, which can pulse to ignite flammable objects nearby.

This mech's name comes from a thousand-year-old poem written by a Haspian monk who survived the erasure of his monastery. His religiously-tinged work describes a razor-bodied fiend pulsing with flesh-searing heat as it crushed scorched bodies under massive claws. The few who have faced a diabolus and survived tend to agree with this depiction.

Even more than other mechanoids, the war queen resembles a giant, living insect. All war mechs can be terrifying, but humans tend to find the war queen disturbing on a deeper level.

The Woolly Stegosaurus finds their home in cold biomes, preferring to eat low-lying vegetation due to a short neck and small head. The spines on the end of the tail differ from the regular Stegosaurus, in that they are curved instead of straight. While this does hinder their ability to defend against predators somewhat, they are much better suited to digging into hard soil and flinging it away to exposed nutritious roots.

rows.label: thrumbo
rows.desc:
A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. The thrumbo is gentle by nature, but extremely dangerous when enraged. While its long fur is exceptionally beautiful, its hide is also incredibly resistant to damage. Its razor-sharp horn fetches a huge price.

Legends say that an old thrumbo is the wisest creature in the universe - it simply chooses not to speak.

rows.label: toxbear
rows.desc:
The Toxbear is a monstrous and deadly creature born from a polluted environment. Standing at an immense size, this mutated bear is a force to be reckoned with. With no natural predators, it roams and hunts at will, leaving destruction in its wake. Its aggressive behavior is fueled by cancerous growth around its head, making it nearly impervious to damage.

As the growth puts pressure on its brain, the Toxbear becomes increasingly violent, eventually turning completely rabid. Not long after that, toxbears are known to try and scratch their own brains out, resulting in their violent demise.

rows.label: patriarch
rows.desc: The gargantuan patriarch of the Sorne geneline serves as the primary male responsible for the survival and protection of the royal caste. His immense digger claws, essential for both hive construction and defense, double as formidable shields capable of absorbing extraordinary amounts of damage. Mounted on his back are vast insect jelly sacks, which provide the resources necessary for rapidly constructing any hive defenses. In battle, his sets of extremely sharp ripper blades and razor-sharp mandibles can efficiently dispatch any threat to the hive. The Patriarch possesses the ability to summon royal caste insectoids from deep underground tunnels, enabling reinforcements to swiftly emerge onto the surface. Upon death, it’s possible to extract a Sorne pherocore from his body.

rows.label: titantick
rows.desc: An incredibly rare and monstrously large insectoid of the Nuchadus geneline, the titantick is a formidable engineered tick, designed to serve as a mobile fuel depot on the harsh magma planet of Nuchadus. This creature features an enormous chemfuel sack attached to its lower abdomen, which is prone to leaking vast quantities of fuel when damaged. In addition to its capacity to store fuel, the titantick can also project streams of burning chemfuel over long distances, making it a dangerous adversary in combat. The volatile nature of its fuel sack means that upon death, the titantick will explode spectacularly, but it’s still possible to extract a Nuchadus pherocore from his body.

rows.label: rock troll
rows.desc:
The rock troll is a colossal, eyeless creature often found living in caves and underground chasms. Much more reclusive than its northern cousins, the rock troll will only surface from its underground lair when provoked.

Lacking regenerative abilities, the rock troll makes up for it through a strange process known as self-petrification. Any open wound will almost immediately be closed by ultra-fast blood clotting that ossifies soon after, creating dense stone-like formations that provide the beast with temporary ablative armor.

rows.label: thrumhorse
rows.desc:
A very nice combination of two highly adaptive baseline creatures which arguably results in the best riding companion man could ask for. While this isn’t apparent in their speed, it definitely is so once a rider experiences the thundering beats of this horsey positively barreling through entire forests and marshland in order to earn its next sugar cube the size of a fist.

A colossal hybrid with recessive equine genes. While they have a lower muscle-to-fat ratio compared to their progenitor, the overall placement and shape of the horn vastly reduces their combat efficiency. Instead, they more than make up for this shortfall with an incredible endurance even compared to paragons. An excellent riding companion that is easier to train and can even carry an acceptable amount of luggage, the majority of which contains feed.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM. Always starts as draftable, even if not using a controller booster to create it. Charge ability: when drafted, the player can use the charge ability to make the hybrid jump towards a target and cause massive damage with its horn to a single random body part. The ability can be triggered every 2 hours.

rows.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09546-1995 [GIGANOTOSAURUS CAROLINII] CODENAME: WRATH >593

A remarkably sized theropod often described as one of the largest known terrestrial predators. With an incredible bite force, teeth for slicing flesh and the ability to sprint large distances at quite the speed, this predator is one to be feared. Gigantosaurus are thankfully solitary creatures for most of their lives, staking territory for themselves, and hunt with fierce abandon. A wide variety of prey often ends up between their jaws. Pray it won't be you next.

rows.desc: A massive and lumbering alien beast capable of rending steel and biting through concrete. It is EXTREMELY dangerous and is best dealt with using explosives and AT weapons, or better-yet landmines.

rows.label: Warbird
rows.desc:
A general-purpose fighter plane, the Warbird is an incredibly fast and effective attack craft. With minimal cargo intended for holding maintenance equipment and fuel, its primary purpose is to engage other aircraft and initiate strafing manoeuvres.

Different to other tier 2 vehicles, this has regular fuel efficiency on the world map but moves significantly faster in return.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when on the move.

<color=#bb8f04>Crew:</color> Pilot x1
<color=#bb8f04>Fuel type:</color> Chemfuel
rows.hitsNote: no melee tools at all — it cannot hurt a pawn by hitting it

specials.text: a vehicle — burns fuel to move
a vehicle that can launch off the map

rows.diet: nothing — it does not eat

rows.label: mechathrumbo
rows.desc:
This hulking cybernetic behemoth is why you don't need tanks in the Rim. Its huge plasteel carapace hides a miniaturized synchrotron that constantly generates small amounts of antimatter, which is instantly used to fill a miniature antigrain warhead. Slow, but quite effective.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color>Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, making the mechathrumbo effective mobile artillery. Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

specials.text: spawns already carrying a permanent condition
dies unless its genetic timer is reset

It is so massive that even giant ground sloths have a place on its menu.

Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest snake ever discovered, Titanoboa, is capable of swallowing cows whole. It can kill even medium-sized animals in just seconds, and thus should be stayed away from at all costs.

rows.label: mecha-muffalo
rows.desc:
This hulking cybernetic organism has been reinforced with an adaptive plasteel mesh, enabling it to carry an incredible amount of stuff. The mecha-muffalo is the perfect pack animal, but it is quite useless in an offensive role. Defensively, however, it is armed with a smoke cannon that it can use to cover the battlefield in a dense cloud of dust.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, making the mecha-muffalo capable of laying a screen of smoke for defensive purposes. Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

rows.desc: The apex of the Naboo core: a grey, lion-faced swimming quadruped the length of a cargo hauler, mammalian and warm-blooded and utterly unhurried. It takes colo claw fish the way a diver takes a ration bar. There is always a bigger fish; this is it.

rows.label: paraceratherium
rows.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest land mammal known to man, Paraceratherium, is a gentle creature, however its size alone can also make it quite a formidable foe to face.
Feeds on plants and trees, which it can easily reach with its extraordinarily long neck, the trait that makes it unique to other genera of rhinoceroses.

specials.text: can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, trees, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: archocentipede
rows.desc:
The Archocentipede is the end result of the Archotech Project, aiming to provide a "friendly" machine superintelligence with a capable body. Even though this centipede is forcefully loyal to the colonists, and can be somewhat controlled by them, most other inhabitants of the planet will consider its existence to be an abomination, since dabbling in archotech usually signals the end of comprehensible human life.

Useful abilities: What do you mean useful? You have WON the game. The Archocentipede is basically unkillable by normal means, just use it to lay waste to everything on the planet. You don't have enemies now, you have pets. Ooooor... the archotech may kill all your colonists. One of the two.

Based on concept art for the Nydus Worm by Federico Dallocchio from Blizzard Entertainment at the Starcraft wiki, https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Nydus_worm/Development.

rows.desc: A scarred bull sando, barnacle-crusted, carrying old harpoon wounds it has outlived by a century. One per sea, if that. Named by every crew that has seen it and survived, which is how it came to have so many names.

rows.label: reefback
rows.desc: So old the reef grows on it: coral, kelp, a hundred hangers-on that never leave. A moving ecosystem, and the one place in the deep where a crew can rest in the light of something else's garden — as long as nobody puts a harpoon in the garden.
rows.diet: nothing — it does not eat

rows.label: starmaw
rows.desc: A filter-feeder the size of a hull, spotted in bioluminescent patterns that read like a night sky when it rises. Sailors navigate by it, and by the crews that vanished trying to.
rows.diet: nothing — it does not eat

rows.label: lanternwhale
rows.desc: Moss-shrouded and trailing blue lantern tendrils that draw the plankton it strains, the lanternwhale is the largest living thing in the seas. It does not notice you. That is the whole of its character, until you make it.
rows.diet: nothing — it does not eat
